```python
        self.play(Write(curve_label))
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 2. Add divisor points to the curve
        # Divisors are formal sums of points with integer coefficients
        self.play(FadeOut(curve_label))
        divisor_label = Text("Divisors: Points with weights", color=WHITE).scale(0.6).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(divisor_label))
        
        # Create 4 divisor points at different angles
        divisors = VGroup()
        for i, angle in enumerate([0, PI/2, PI, 3*PI/2]):

            label = Text(f"P{i+1}", color=WHITE).scale(0.4).next_to(point, UP * 0.5)
            
            # Alternate between positive and negative weights
            # These weights represent the multiplicity of each point in the divisor
            weight_val = 1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1
            weight = Text(f"{weight_val}", color=GREEN if weight_val > 0 else RED).scale(0.4)
            weight.next_to(point, DOWN * 0.5)
            
            divisor_group = VGroup(point, label, weight)
            divisors.add(divisor_group)
            self.play(Create(point), Write(label), Write(weight), run_time=0.7)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 3. Show linear systems
        # A linear system is a family of divisors that are linearly equivalent
        self.play(FadeOut(divisor_label))
        linear_label = Text("Linear Systems", color=WHITE).scale(0.6).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(linear_label))
        
        # Create two additional offset curves to represent the linear system
        curve2 = Circle(radius=2.1, color=BLUE_C).stretch(0.53, 1).set_opacity(0.6)
        curve3 = Circle(radius=1.9, color=BLUE_D).stretch(0.47, 1).set_opacity(0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(curve2), Create(curve3))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 4. Show global sections as connecting lines
        # Global sections are the elements of the vector space associated with a divisor
        self.play(FadeOut(linear_label))
        section_label = Text("Global Sections", color=WHITE).scale(0.6).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(section_label))
        
        # Create lines connecting points on different curves
        lines = VGroup()
        for angle in [PI/4, 3*PI/4, 5*PI/4, 7*PI/4]:
            p1 = curve.point_at_angle(angle)
            p2 = curve2.point_at_angle(angle)
            p3 = curve3.point_at_angle(angle)
            
            line1 = Line(p1, p2, color=YELLOW, stroke_opacity=0.7)
            line2 = Line(p1, p3, color=YELLOW, stroke_opacity=0.7)
            
            lines.add(line1, line2)
            self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 5. Highlight specific sections to demonstrate the theorem
        # These glowing paths represent how the sections are related to divisor degree
        for i in range(2):
            self.play(lines[i].animate.set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(width=4))
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 6. Show the Riemann-Roch equations
        # These equations express the relationship between divisors and their sections
        self.play(FadeOut(section_label))
        theorem_label = Text("Riemann-Roch Theorem", color=WHITE).scale(0.6).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(theorem_label))
        
        # First equation: l(D) = deg(D) - g + 1
        # l(D) is dimension of global sections, g is genus
        eq1 = Text("l(D) = deg(D) - g + 1", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        eq1.next_to(theorem_label, DOWN * 2)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Second equation: l(D) - l(K-D) = deg(D) - g + 1
        # K is the canonical divisor
        eq2 = Text("l(D) - l(K-D) = deg(D) - g + 1", color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        eq2.next_to(eq1, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(eq2))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # 7. Conclusion
        self.play(FadeOut(theorem_label), FadeOut(eq1), FadeOut(eq2))
        
        conclusion = Text("The harmony of algebraic curves", color=WHITE).scale(0.6).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final fade out of all elements
        all_objects = VGroup(curve, curve2, curve3, divisors, lines, conclusion)
        self.play(FadeOut(all_objects))
```

```python
from manim import *
import math

class ModularInverseVisualization(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Visualizing Modular Inverses", font_size=36)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Definition of modular inverse
        definition = MathTex(r"ax \equiv 1 \pmod{m}")
        self.play(Write(definition))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Condition for existence
        condition = MathTex(r"\gcd(a, m) = 1")
        condition_text = Text("Exists if and only if:", font_size=24)
        condition_text.next_to(definition, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        condition.next_to(condition_text, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(Write(condition_text))
        self.play(Write(condition))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        self.play(FadeOut(definition), FadeOut(condition_text), FadeOut(condition))
        
        # Example with modulus 8
        m = 8
        example_title = Text(f"Modular Inverses in mod {m}", font_size=28)
        example_title.to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(example_title))
        
        # Create a visual representation of the modular system
        number_circles = VGroup()
        circle_radius = 0.5
        
        for i in range(m):
            circle = Circle(radius=circle_radius, color=WHITE)
            # Arrange in a circle
            angle = i * TAU / m
            circle_pos = 3 * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            circle.move_to(circle_pos)
            
            number = Text(str(i), font_size=24)
            number.move_to(circle.get_center())
            number_circles.add(VGroup(circle, number))
        
        self.play(Create(number_circles))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Check which numbers have inverses
        explanation_text = Text("", font_size=20)
        explanation_text.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # Highlight each number and check its GCD with the modulus
        for i in range(m):
            # Skip 0 which never has an inverse
            if i == 0:
                gcd_val = m
                has_inverse = False
            else:
                gcd_val = math.gcd(i, m)
                has_inverse = (gcd_val == 1)
            
            # Find the inverse if it exists
            inverse = None
            if has_inverse:
                for j in range(1, m):
                    if (i * j) % m == 1:
                        inverse = j
                        break
            
            # Update the explanation
            if has_inverse:
                new_explanation = Text(
                    f"gcd({i}, {m}) = 1, {i} has inverse: {inverse}",
                    font_size=20, color=GREEN
                )
                circle_color = GREEN
            else:
                new_explanation = Text(
                    f"gcd({i}, {m}) = {gcd_val} ≠ 1, No inverse",
                    font_size=20, color=RED
                )
                circle_color = RED
            
            # Highlight the current circle
            self.play(
                number_circles[i][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=3),
                FadeOut(explanation_text),
                run_time=0.3
            )
            
            explanation_text = new_explanation
            explanation_text.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(
                Write(explanation_text),
                number_circles[i][0].animate.set_fill(circle_color, opacity=0.3),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            
            # Reset highlight but keep the fill color
            self.play(
                number_circles[i][0].animate.set_stroke(WHITE, width=1),
                run_time=0.2
            )
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Connect the numbers with lines based on common factors
        connections_text = Text(
            "Numbers without inverses share common factors with the modulus",
            font_size=20
        )
        connections_text.next_to(explanation_text, UP, buff=0.3)
        self.play(Write(connections_text))
        
        # Draw lines between numbers with common factors (other than 1)
        lines = []
        
        # Connect numbers that share factors with the modulus
        for i in range(1, m):
            if math.gcd(i, m) > 1:
                # Draw line from 0 (representing the modulus) to i
                line = Line(
                    number_circles[0].get_center(),
                    number_circles[i].get_center(),
                    color=YELLOW
                )
                lines.append(line)
        
        self.play(*[Create(line) for line in lines], run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        self.play(
            FadeOut(number_circles),
            *[FadeOut(line) for line in lines],
            FadeOut(connections_text),
            FadeOut(explanation_text),
            FadeOut(example_title)
        )
        
        conclusion = Text(
            "A number has a modular inverse if and only if\n"
            "it is coprime with the modulus (gcd = 1).",
            font_size=28
        )
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(conclusion))
```

```python
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Define Event A as a subset", seconds=4)
    def show_event_a(self):
        # Event A: top two rows (8 outcomes)
        self.event_a_indices = list(range(8))
        
        anim_group = []
        for i in self.event_a_indices:
            anim_group.append(self.grid[i].animate.set_fill(GREEN_E, opacity=0.6).set_stroke(GREEN_C))

        self.play(Write(label_a), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1.0)

    @beat("State probability of A fraction", seconds=4)
    def compute_p_a(self):
        total = len(self.grid)
        count_a = len(self.event_a_indices)
        frac = Fraction(count_a, total)
        
        formula = MathTex(
            f"P(A) = \\frac{{{count_a}}}{{{total}}} = {frac}",
            font_size=40
        ).move_to([3.5, 1.0, 0])
        
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Introduce Event B and condition on it", seconds=4)
    def show_event_b_conditioning(self):
        # Event B: right two columns (indices where col % 4 >= 2) -> columns 2 and 3
        # Grid is 4x4: rows 0-3, cols 0-3. Indices:
        # Col 2,3 in row 0: 2, 3
        # Col 2,3 in row 1: 6, 7
        # Col 2,3 in row 2: 10, 11
        # Col 2,3 in row 3: 14, 15
        self.event_b_indices = [2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15]
        
        # Dim non-B elements, highlight intersection (A and B)
        anim_group = []
        for i, square in enumerate(self.grid):
            if i in self.event_b_indices and i in self.event_a_indices:
                # Intersection: top-right 2x2
                anim_group.append(square.animate.set_fill(YELLOW_E, opacity=0.8).set_stroke(YELLOW_C))
            elif i in self.event_b_indices:
                # Only B
                anim_group.append(square.animate.set_fill(PURPLE_E, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(PURPLE_C))

                # Outside B

        self.play(AnimationGroup(*anim_group, run_time=2.5))
        self.play(FadeIn(label_cond, shift=UP), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Compute conditional probability", seconds=4)
    def compute_conditional(self):
        intersection_count = len([i for i in self.event_b_indices if i in self.event_a_indices])
        b_count = len(self.event_b_indices)
        cond_frac = Fraction(intersection_count, b_count)

        cond_formula = MathTex(

            font_size=42,
            color=YELLOW_C
        ).move_to([3.5, -1.0, 0])

        self.play(Write(cond_formula), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(2.0)
```

```python
from manim import *

class MSTPrimVsKruskal(Scene):

        # Title
        title = Text("Unraveling the Mysteries of Minimum Spanning Trees", font_size=32)
        title.to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Create two simple graphs side by side
        # Dense graph (left)
        dense_nodes = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            angle = i * PI/2
            node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE).move_to([-3 + 1.2*np.cos(angle), 0 + 1.2*np.sin(angle), 0])
            dense_nodes.add(node)
        
        center_node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE).move_to([-3, 0, 0])
        dense_nodes.add(center_node)
        
        dense_edges = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            # Connect center to all nodes
            edge = Line(center_node.get_center(), dense_nodes[i].get_center(), color=WHITE)
            dense_edges.add(edge)
            # Connect nodes in a circle
            next_node = dense_nodes[(i+1) % 4]
            edge = Line(dense_nodes[i].get_center(), next_node.get_center(), color=WHITE)
            dense_edges.add(edge)
        
        dense_graph = VGroup(dense_nodes, dense_edges)
        
        # Sparse graph (right)
        sparse_nodes = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            angle = i * PI/2
            node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN).move_to([3 + 1.2*np.cos(angle), 0 + 1.2*np.sin(angle), 0])
            sparse_nodes.add(node)
        
        center_node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN).move_to([3, 0, 0])
        sparse_nodes.add(center_node)
        
        sparse_edges = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            # Only connect center to all nodes
            edge = Line(center_node.get_center(), sparse_nodes[i].get_center(), color=WHITE)
            sparse_edges.add(edge)
        
        sparse_graph = VGroup(sparse_nodes, sparse_edges)
        
        # Labels
        dense_label = Text("Dense Graph", font_size=24, color=BLUE).next_to(dense_graph, UP)
        sparse_label = Text("Sparse Graph", font_size=24, color=GREEN).next_to(sparse_graph, UP)
        
        # Show both graphs
        self.play(
            Create(dense_graph),
            Create(sparse_graph),
            Write(dense_label),
            Write(sparse_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Prim's Algorithm
        prim_label = Text("Prim's Algorithm", font_size=28)
        prim_label.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.5)
        self.play(Write(prim_label))
        
        # Highlight starting node for Prim's (center node)
        self.play(
            dense_nodes[4].animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8),
            sparse_nodes[4].animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
        )
        
        # Show a few steps of Prim's on both graphs
        # For dense graph - highlight 3 edges and nodes
        for i in range(3):
            self.play(
                dense_edges[i].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
                dense_nodes[i].animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
            )
        
        # For sparse graph - highlight all 4 edges and nodes
        for i in range(4):
            self.play(
                sparse_edges[i].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
                sparse_nodes[i].animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
            )
        
        # Show complexity
        prim_eq = Text("O(E log V) for dense graph", font_size=24)
        prim_eq2 = Text("O(V²) for sparse graph", font_size=24)

        )
        
        # Kruskal's Algorithm
        kruskal_label = Text("Kruskal's Algorithm", font_size=28)
        kruskal_label.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1.5)

        for i in [1, 3, 5]:
```

```python
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro_text))
        
        # Create a simple pendulum visualization
        pivot = Dot(point=UP*2, color=BLUE)  # Pivot point (fixed)
        bob = Dot(point=UP*1, color=RED)     # Bob (the weight at the end)
        string = Line(pivot.get_center(), bob.get_center(), color=WHITE)  # String connecting pivot to bob
        pendulum = VGroup(string, bob)  # Group the string and bob together
        
        pendulum_label = Text("Simple Pendulum", font_size=20)
        pendulum_label.next_to(pendulum, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # Display the pendulum
        self.play(Create(pivot), Create(pendulum), Write(pendulum_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show the key equation relating period to length
        equation = MathTex(r"T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}")
        equation.shift(DOWN)
        
        eq_explanation = Text("Period (T) depends on length (L) and gravity (g)", font_size=20)
        eq_explanation.next_to(equation, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_explanation))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Clear the screen for the next part
        self.play(
            FadeOut(pendulum), 
            FadeOut(pivot), 
            FadeOut(pendulum_label), 
            FadeOut(eq_explanation)
        )
        self.play(equation.animate.to_edge(UP), FadeOut(title))
        
        # Create three pendulums with exponentially increasing lengths
        pendulums = VGroup()
        lengths = [1, 2, 4]  # Length increases exponentially (1, 2, 4)
        spacing = 3  # Horizontal spacing between pendulums
        
        for i, length in enumerate(lengths):
            # Create pivot, bob, and string for each pendulum
            p_pivot = Dot(point=UP*2 + RIGHT*(i-1)*spacing, color=BLUE)
            p_bob = Dot(point=p_pivot.get_center() + DOWN*length, color=RED)
            p_string = Line(p_pivot.get_center(), p_bob.get_center(), color=WHITE)
            
            # Label showing the length
            p_label = Text(f"Length = {length}", font_size=16)
            p_label.next_to(p_bob, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            
            # Calculate and show the period using the formula T = 2π√(L/g)
            period_value = round(2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(length / 9.8), 2)  # Using g=9.8 m/s²
            period_text = Text(f"Period = {period_value}s", font_size=16)
            period_text.next_to(p_label, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            
            # Group all elements of this pendulum
            p_group = VGroup(p_pivot, p_string, p_bob, p_label, period_text)
            pendulums.add(p_group)
        
        # Display all three pendulums
        self.play(Create(pendulums))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Show the key insight about the relationship
        insight_text = Text("As length increases exponentially, period grows with square root", font_size=24)
        insight_text.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        self.play(Write(insight_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Conclusion
        self.play(FadeOut(pendulums), FadeOut(equation), FadeOut(insight_text))
        conclusion = Text("The elegance of dynamical systems reveals itself in pendulum motion", font_size=28)
        conclusion.move_to(ORIGIN)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(conclusion))
```

```python
"""Gold scene 002 — learning rate and gradient descent.

The whole scene is driven by ``forge.primitives.optimise.Descent``. Nothing
about any trajectory is authored: the ball goes where the update rule sends it,
the divergence diverges because the arithmetic diverges, and the reported final
positions are read off the run rather than typed in.

That is the property worth training on. A model that learns to draw a plausible
descent curve has learned decoration. A model that learns to *run the optimiser
and animate the result* has learned something true.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.optimise import Descent, minimum_of

CURVE_C = BLUE_C
BALL_C = YELLOW_C
GOOD_C = "#5CD0B3"
BAD_C = "#FC6255"
SLOW_C = "#F0AC5F"

X_LO, X_HI = -5.0, 5.0


def loss(x: float) -> float:
    return 0.35 * x ** 2 + 0.4 * x + 1.2


class LearningRate(ForgeScene):

    x0 = 3.4

    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------------

    def make_axes(self) -> Axes:
        return Axes(
            x_range=[X_LO, X_HI, 1], y_range=[0, 11, 2],
            x_length=7.4, y_length=4.9,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2,
                         "color": GREY_B, "font_size": 20},
        ).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.35)

    def on_curve(self, x: float):
        return self.axes.c2p(x, loss(x))

    def run_descent(self, lr: float, n: int = 14) -> Descent:
        return Descent(loss, x0=self.x0, lr=lr, n_steps=n)

    def panel_text(self, *lines, color=WHITE, size=26) -> VGroup:
        return VGroup(*[Text(l, font_size=size, color=color) for l in lines]) \
            .arrange(DOWN, buff=0.16, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 1.4, 0])

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw the loss curve and mark its true minimum", seconds=5)
    def setup_curve(self):
        self.axes = self.make_axes()
        self.curve = self.axes.plot(loss, x_range=[X_LO, X_HI], color=CURVE_C,
                                    stroke_width=4)
        self.title = Text("Gradient descent", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)

        min_x, min_y = minimum_of(loss, X_LO, X_HI)     # found, not assumed
        self.min_dot = Dot(self.axes.c2p(min_x, min_y), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.07)
        # Below the x-axis, not between dot and axis: the curve's minimum sits
        # close enough to y=0 that a label placed under the dot lands on the
        # tick marks.
        self.min_label = Text("minimum", font_size=20, color=GOOD_C)
        self.min_label.next_to(self.axes.c2p(min_x, 0), DOWN, buff=0.28)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), Create(self.axes), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=1.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.min_dot, scale=0.5), Write(self.min_label), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Place a ball on the slope and show the gradient", seconds=5)
    def show_gradient(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        g = d.steps[0].grad

        self.ball = Dot(self.on_curve(self.x0), color=BALL_C, radius=0.11)
        span = 1.15
        tangent = Line(
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 - span, loss(self.x0) - g * span),
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 + span, loss(self.x0) + g * span),
            color=BALL_C, stroke_width=3,
        )

        self.rule = self.panel_text("the slope tells you", "which way is downhill",
                                    color=GREY_B, size=23)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.ball, scale=0.4), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Create(tangent), FadeIn(self.rule, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(0.6)
        self.play(FadeOut(tangent), FadeOut(self.rule), run_time=0.5)

    @beat("A good learning rate walks the ball to the minimum", seconds=8)
    def good_rate(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.55", color=GOOD_C, size=30)
        self.play(FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.6)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps[:10]:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.045).set_opacity(0.55)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(
                self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.28, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine,
            )

        verdict = Text(f"settles at x = {d.final_x:.2f}", font_size=24, color=GOOD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too large a step and it climbs out of the valley", seconds=8)
    def too_large(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=3.5)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "3.5", color=BAD_C, size=30)

        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        # Only the steps still inside the frame can be drawn; the rest is the point.
        visible = [s for s in d.steps if X_LO < s.next_x < X_HI][:6]
        for s in visible:
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      run_time=0.32, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine)

        arrow = Arrow(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 1.4, 8.2), self.axes.c2p(X_HI, 10.4),
                      color=BAD_C, buff=0, stroke_width=5)
        gone = Text("off the chart", font_size=22, color=BAD_C).next_to(arrow, LEFT, buff=0.12)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 0.2, 10.0)).set_opacity(0.3),
                  GrowArrow(arrow), FadeIn(gone), run_time=0.9)

        verdict = Text(f"reaches x = {d.final_x:,.0f}", font_size=24, color=BAD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(gone), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict),
                  self.ball.animate.set_opacity(1.0), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too small and it never arrives", seconds=7)
    def too_small(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.15)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.15", color=SLOW_C, size=30)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=SLOW_C, radius=0.04).set_opacity(0.5)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.2)

        verdict = Text(f"only x = {d.final_x:.2f} after {len(d.steps)} steps",
                       font_size=22, color=SLOW_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("The three rates side by side", seconds=6)
    def compare(self):
        rows = VGroup()
        for lr, colour, note in ((0.15, SLOW_C, "too small"),
                                 (0.55, GOOD_C, "about right"),
                                 (3.5, BAD_C, "too large")):
            d = self.run_descent(lr)
            rows.add(VGroup(
                Text(f"{lr}", font_size=26, color=colour),
                Text(note, font_size=20, color=GREY_B),
            ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN))
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.34, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=RIGHT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.25, run_time=1.6))
        self.play(Indicate(rows[1], color=GOOD_C, scale_factor=1.12), run_time=0.9)
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
def MathOperation(path, expression_text):
    image = ImageMobject(path)
    expression = Tex(expression_text, color=BLACK)
    expression.scale(1.8)
    group = Group(image, expression)
    group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25)

    return group

def LetterOperation(expression, expression_result):
    inner_group = Group(
        Tex(expression, color=TEXT_COLOR).scale(1.8),
        Tex(expression_result, color=TEXT_COLOR).scale(1.8),
    ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.8)
    box = DashedVMobject(
        SurroundingRectangle(inner_group, color=AQUA_BLUE_COLOR, buff=0.5),
        num_dashes=25,
        dashed_ratio=0.7
    )
    outer_group = Group(
        box,
        inner_group
    )

    return outer_group
```

```python
        # Highlight diagonal digits

        diagonal_digits = []

            digit_pos = 3 + i  # "n: 0." is 3 characters, then we add i
            highlight = Square(side_length=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
            highlight.move_to(row[digit_pos])
            diagonal.add(highlight)
            diagonal_digits.append(number_strings[i][i+2])  # i+2 because we skip "0."

            # Highlight the changed digit
            new_highlight = Square(side_length=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.3)
            new_highlight.move_to(diagonal[i])
```

```python
"""Gold scene 001 — rook mobility and corner probability.

Authored by hand from Nimit's own prompt:

    "build me a chess grid, add rooks on it and animate the rook's possible
     movements, then help me calculate the probability that if i place the
     rook at any square, it is a corner square"

This is a *target*, not a sample: the standard the fine-tuned model has to
reach. Two properties make it gold rather than merely working.

**Every number on screen is computed.** The 4, the 64 and the 1/16 come from
counting cells in ``forge.primitives.grid``. Nothing here recites a figure a
language model happened to remember.

**It answers more than it was asked.** The prompt requested rook movement and
corner probability as two separate things. Beat 4 finds the link worth showing:
a rook reaches exactly 14 squares from *every* square on the board, corners
included. That invariance came out of writing the primitive, and it is the
difference between a diagram and an explanation.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.grid import Board, Cell

# A restrained palette: neutral board, one colour for attention, one for the
# result. Loud boards fight the thing you are trying to point at.
LIGHT_SQ = "#3D4852"
DARK_SQ = "#2A313A"
ROOK_C = BLUE_C
REACH_C = YELLOW_C
CORNER_C = "#5CD0B3"

CELL = 0.70
BOARD_X = -3.1      # board centre; right half is the information panel
PANEL_X = 3.4


def rook_glyph(color=ROOK_C) -> VGroup:
    """A rook built from primitives rather than a font glyph — no typeface to
    be missing, and it scales cleanly."""
    base = Rectangle(width=0.40, height=0.07, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem = Rectangle(width=0.24, height=0.24, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    head = Rectangle(width=0.36, height=0.10, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem.next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
    head.next_to(stem, UP, buff=0)
    return VGroup(base, stem, head)


class RookCorners(ForgeScene):

    board = Board(8, 8)

    # -- geometry helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def xy(self, cell: Cell) -> np.ndarray:
        """Cell -> world coordinates, with the board centred on the origin."""
        x = BOARD_X + (cell.col - (self.board.cols - 1) / 2) * CELL
        y = (cell.row - (self.board.rows - 1) / 2) * CELL - 0.3
        return np.array([x, y, 0.0])

    def tile(self, cell: Cell, color, opacity=0.85) -> Square:
        return Square(side_length=CELL, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=color, fill_opacity=opacity).move_to(self.xy(cell))

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw an 8x8 chessboard", seconds=3)
    def draw_board(self):
        self.squares = VGroup(*[
            self.tile(c, LIGHT_SQ if self.board.is_light(c) else DARK_SQ, 1.0)
            for c in self.board.cells()
        ])
        self.title = Text("A rook on an 8 x 8 board", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s, scale=0.6) for s in self.squares],
                              lag_ratio=0.012, run_time=2.0))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)

    @beat("Place a rook on d4", seconds=2)
    def place_rook(self):
        self.origin = Cell(3, 3)                      # d4
        self.rook = rook_glyph().move_to(self.xy(self.origin))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.rook, shift=UP * 0.4), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(self.rook, color=ROOK_C, line_length=0.16, num_lines=10,
                        flash_radius=0.42), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight every square the rook can reach", seconds=5)
    def show_reach(self):
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(self.origin)     # computed, not hardcoded
        self.reach_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.count = VGroup(
            Text(str(len(reach)), font_size=72, color=REACH_C),
            Text("reachable squares", font_size=24, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.18).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t) for t in self.reach_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.05, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.count[0], scale=0.7), Write(self.count[1]), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.4)

    @beat("Move the rook to the corner - the count is unchanged", seconds=5)
    def corner_is_no_different(self):
        corner = Cell(0, 0)                            # a1
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(corner)
        new_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.play(
            self.rook.animate.move_to(self.xy(corner)),
            Transform(self.reach_tiles, new_tiles),
            run_time=1.6,
        )
        # The count is unchanged, so the numeral must visibly hold still while
        # everything around it moves — that stillness *is* the point of the beat.
        self.play(Indicate(self.count[0], color=REACH_C, scale_factor=1.25), run_time=0.8)

        note = VGroup(
            Text("still 14.", font_size=28, color=REACH_C),
            Text("a rook's reach is the", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
            Text("same from every square", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.12).move_to([PANEL_X, -1.5, 0])
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.9)
        self.play(FadeOut(note), FadeOut(self.reach_tiles), FadeOut(self.count),
                  run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight the four corner squares", seconds=4)
    def show_corners(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()                 # computed -> 4
        self.corner_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, CORNER_C, 0.55) for c in corners])

        new_title = Text("How likely is a corner?", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(Transform(self.title, new_title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rook, shift=DOWN * 0.3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(t) for t in self.corner_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.4))
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Derive the probability as an exact fraction", seconds=6)
    def derive(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()
        p = self.board.probability_of(corners)         # Fraction(1, 16) - exact

        expr = MathTex(
            r"P(\text{corner})", "=",
            rf"\frac{{{len(corners)}}}{{{self.board.n_cells}}}",
            font_size=42,
        ).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])
        expr[2].set_color(CORNER_C)

        reduced = MathTex("=", rf"\frac{{{p.numerator}}}{{{p.denominator}}}", font_size=52)
        reduced[1].set_color(CORNER_C)
        reduced.next_to(expr, DOWN, buff=0.45)

        self.play(Write(expr[0]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Write(expr[1]), Write(expr[2]), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(reduced), run_time=0.9)

        pct = Text(f"{float(p) * 100:.2f}%", font_size=26, color=GREY_B)
        pct.next_to(reduced, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(pct, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.6)
        self.expr, self.reduced, self.pct = expr, reduced, pct
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
    def show_refraction(self):

        # Let's compute refracted angle using Snell's Law: n1 * sin(theta1) = n2 * sin(theta2)
        n1 = 1.0
        n2 = 1.5
        # Incident angle theta1 = arccos(dot(UP, -v_inc))
        v_inc = (self.p_start - self.p_origin)
        v_inc = v_inc / np.linalg.norm(v_inc)
        cos_i = np.dot(UP, -v_inc)
        sin_i = np.sqrt(max(0.0, 1.0 - cos_i**2))
        
        sin_r = (n1 / n2) * sin_i
        theta_r = np.arcsin(sin_r)
        
        # Direction vector in glass (going down and right, but steeper down along -UP)
        # angle from downward normal (DOWN) is theta_r
        dx = np.sin(theta_r) * np.sign(-v_inc[0]) # keep same side
        dy = -np.cos(theta_r)
        v_ref = np.array([dx, dy, 0.0])
        
        self.p_end = self.p_origin + v_ref * 3.75
        self.refracted_ray = Arrow(
            self.p_origin, self.p_end, 
            buff=0, color=RED_C, stroke_width=4
        )
        self.refracted_label = Text("Refracted Ray", font_size=20, color=RED_C).move_to(np.array([1.8, -1.5, 0]))

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(self.refracted_ray),
            FadeIn(self.refracted_label),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(2.5)

    @beat("Highlight the angle of refraction", seconds=4)
    def show_refraction_angle(self):
        # Arc for refracted angle between DOWN vector and refracted ray
        v_ref = (self.p_end - self.p_origin)
        v_ref = v_ref / np.linalg.norm(v_ref)
        
        cos_r = np.dot(DOWN, v_ref)
        theta_r = np.arccos(cos_r)
        
        self.angle_r_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.7,
            start_angle=-np.pi/2,
            angle=theta_r if v_ref[0] > 0 else -theta_r,
            color=RED_C
        )
        
        self.label_r = MathTex(r"\theta_2", color=RED_C, font_size=28).move_to(np.array([0.4, -0.6, 0]))

        self.play(
            Create(self.angle_r_arc),
            Write(self.label_r),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(2.0)

    @beat("Introduce Snell's Law equation", seconds=5)
    def show_snells_law(self):
        self.snell_formula = MathTex(
            r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)",
            font_size=36
        ).to_edge(UP).shift(RIGHT * 3.5)
        
        self.play(
            Write(self.snell_formula),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Add a bounding box to emphasize the formula
        self.formula_box = SurroundingRectangle(self.snell_formula, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(self.formula_box), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(2.0)

    @beat("Explain why it bends: wave wavefront view", seconds=5)
    def explain_speed_change(self):
        # Show wavefronts slowing down on entering the medium
        self.explanation_text = Text(
            "Light slows down in denser medium,\ncausing the wavefronts to pivot.",
            font_size=20,

        ).to_edge(DOWN).shift(RIGHT * 3)

        # Draw a few parallel wavefront lines perpendicular to the incident ray

        wf1 = Line(np.array([-2.5, 3.5, 0]), np.array([-3.5, 2.5, 0]), color=YELLOW_E, stroke_width=2)
        wf2 = Line(np.array([-1.5, 2.5, 0]), np.array([-2.5, 1.5, 0]), color=YELLOW_E, stroke_width=2)

    @beat("Clean up wavefronts and emphasize core takeaway", seconds=4)
```

```python
        p2 = self.origin + self.vec_a + self.vec_b
        p3 = self.origin + self.vec_b

        self.parallelogram = Polygon(

        p_drop = np.array([self.origin[0] + self.vec_b[0], self.origin[1], 0.0])
        p_top = self.origin + self.vec_b

        self.height_line = DashedLine(p_top, p_drop, color=RED_C, stroke_width=3)
        self.height_label = MathTex(

        ).next_to(self.height_line, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.angle_arc = Angle(line_a, line_b, radius=0.65, color=WHITE)

            Write(self.height_label),

    def derive_formula(self):
        title = Text("Parallelogram Area", font_size=32, color=WHITE).move_to(
            [3.2, 2.2, 0]
        )
        eq1 = MathTex(r"\text{Area} = \text{base} \times \text{height}", font_size=30)
        eq2 = MathTex(r"= \|\vec{a}\| \cdot (\|\vec{b}\|\sin\theta)", font_size=30)
        eq3 = MathTex(r"= \|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\|", font_size=34, color=YELLOW_C)

    def compute_numerical_area(self):

        cross_vector = np.cross(self.vec_a, self.vec_b)
        area_val = np.linalg.norm(cross_vector)
        norm_a_val = np.linalg.norm(self.vec_a)

        ).move_to([3.2, -2.0, 0])

        calc_label = VGroup(

                font_size=24,
            ),
            MathTex(
                rf"\text{{Computed Area}} = {area_val:.2f}",
                font_size=30,
                color=GREEN_C,
            ),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25).move_to(calc_box)

        self.play(
            Create(calc_box),
            Write(calc_label),
            self.parallelogram.animate.set_fill(GREEN_D, opacity=0.55),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
```

```python
class MultiplyMatrix(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, matrix_1, matrix_2, element_time=1, run_time=3, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.matrix_1 = matrix_1
        self.matrix_2 = matrix_2

        self.result_matrix = self.get_result_matrix()
```

```python
counting cells in ``forge.primitives.grid``. Nothing here recites a figure a
language model happened to remember.

**It answers more than it was asked.** The prompt requested rook movement and
corner probability as two separate things. Beat 4 finds the link worth showing:

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.grid import Board, Cell

# A restrained palette: neutral board, one colour for attention, one for the
# result. Loud boards fight the thing you are trying to point at.
LIGHT_SQ = "#3D4852"
DARK_SQ = "#2A313A"
ROOK_C = BLUE_C
REACH_C = YELLOW_C
CORNER_C = "#5CD0B3"

CELL = 0.70
BOARD_X = -3.1      # board centre; right half is the information panel
PANEL_X = 3.4


def rook_glyph(color=ROOK_C) -> VGroup:
    """A rook built from primitives rather than a font glyph — no typeface to
    be missing, and it scales cleanly."""
    base = Rectangle(width=0.40, height=0.07, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem = Rectangle(width=0.24, height=0.24, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    head = Rectangle(width=0.36, height=0.10, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem.next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
    head.next_to(stem, UP, buff=0)
    return VGroup(base, stem, head)


class RookCorners(ForgeScene):

    board = Board(8, 8)

    # -- geometry helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def xy(self, cell: Cell) -> np.ndarray:
        """Cell -> world coordinates, with the board centred on the origin."""
        x = BOARD_X + (cell.col - (self.board.cols - 1) / 2) * CELL
        y = (cell.row - (self.board.rows - 1) / 2) * CELL - 0.3
        return np.array([x, y, 0.0])

    def tile(self, cell: Cell, color, opacity=0.85) -> Square:
        return Square(side_length=CELL, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=color, fill_opacity=opacity).move_to(self.xy(cell))

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw an 8x8 chessboard", seconds=3)
    def draw_board(self):
        self.squares = VGroup(*[
            self.tile(c, LIGHT_SQ if self.board.is_light(c) else DARK_SQ, 1.0)
            for c in self.board.cells()
        ])
        self.title = Text("A rook on an 8 x 8 board", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s, scale=0.6) for s in self.squares],
                              lag_ratio=0.012, run_time=2.0))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)

    @beat("Place a rook on d4", seconds=2)
    def place_rook(self):
        self.origin = Cell(3, 3)                      # d4
        self.rook = rook_glyph().move_to(self.xy(self.origin))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.rook, shift=UP * 0.4), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(self.rook, color=ROOK_C, line_length=0.16, num_lines=10,
                        flash_radius=0.42), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight every square the rook can reach", seconds=5)
    def show_reach(self):
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(self.origin)     # computed, not hardcoded
        self.reach_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.count = VGroup(
            Text(str(len(reach)), font_size=72, color=REACH_C),
            Text("reachable squares", font_size=24, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.18).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t) for t in self.reach_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.05, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.count[0], scale=0.7), Write(self.count[1]), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.4)

    @beat("Move the rook to the corner - the count is unchanged", seconds=5)
    def corner_is_no_different(self):
        corner = Cell(0, 0)                            # a1
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(corner)
        new_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.play(
            self.rook.animate.move_to(self.xy(corner)),
            Transform(self.reach_tiles, new_tiles),
            run_time=1.6,
        )
        # The count is unchanged, so the numeral must visibly hold still while
        # everything around it moves — that stillness *is* the point of the beat.
        self.play(Indicate(self.count[0], color=REACH_C, scale_factor=1.25), run_time=0.8)

        note = VGroup(
            Text("still 14.", font_size=28, color=REACH_C),
            Text("a rook's reach is the", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
            Text("same from every square", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.12).move_to([PANEL_X, -1.5, 0])
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.9)
        self.play(FadeOut(note), FadeOut(self.reach_tiles), FadeOut(self.count),
                  run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight the four corner squares", seconds=4)
    def show_corners(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()                 # computed -> 4
        self.corner_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, CORNER_C, 0.55) for c in corners])

        new_title = Text("How likely is a corner?", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(Transform(self.title, new_title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rook, shift=DOWN * 0.3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(t) for t in self.corner_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.4))
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Derive the probability as an exact fraction", seconds=6)
    def derive(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()
        p = self.board.probability_of(corners)         # Fraction(1, 16) - exact

        expr = MathTex(
            r"P(\text{corner})", "=",
            rf"\frac{{{len(corners)}}}{{{self.board.n_cells}}}",
            font_size=42,
        ).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])
        expr[2].set_color(CORNER_C)

        reduced = MathTex("=", rf"\frac{{{p.numerator}}}{{{p.denominator}}}", font_size=52)
        reduced[1].set_color(CORNER_C)
        reduced.next_to(expr, DOWN, buff=0.45)

        self.play(Write(expr[0]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Write(expr[1]), Write(expr[2]), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(reduced), run_time=0.9)

        pct = Text(f"{float(p) * 100:.2f}%", font_size=26, color=GREY_B)
        pct.next_to(reduced, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(pct, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.6)
        self.expr, self.reduced, self.pct = expr, reduced, pct
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
from manim import *
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
import numpy as np

class CompareAndSwapSort(ForgeScene):
    values = [1.5, 3.8, 2.0, 4.2, 2.9]
    idx1, idx2 = 1, 2  # Indices of adjacent elements to compare

    def get_x(self, index):
        return -3.0 + index * 1.5

    def make_bar(self, val, index, color=BLUE_C):
        rect = Rectangle(
            width=1.0,
            height=val,
            fill_opacity=0.85,
            fill_color=color,
            stroke_color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        pos = np.array([self.get_x(index), -1.8 + val / 2.0, 0])
        rect.move_to(pos)
        lbl = DecimalNumber(
            val,
            num_decimal_places=1,
            font_size=24,
            color=WHITE
        ).next_to(rect, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        return VGroup(rect, lbl)

    @beat("Compare adjacent elements in array", seconds=3)
    def compare_elements(self):
        self.bars = VGroup(*[
            self.make_bar(val, i) for i, val in enumerate(self.values)
        ])

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b, shift=UP * 0.3) for b in self.bars], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=1.2
        )

        v1, v2 = self.values[self.idx1], self.values[self.idx2]
        needs_swap = v1 > v2  # dynamically evaluated condition

        highlight1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx1, color=RED_C)
        highlight2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx2, color=RED_C)

        comp_op = ">" if needs_swap else "≤"
        action = "Swap Needed" if needs_swap else "In Order"
        self.cmp_text = Text(
            f"{v1} {comp_op} {v2}  ({action})",
            font_size=28,
            color=RED_C
        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)

        self.play(
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx1], highlight1),
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx2], highlight2),
            Write(self.cmp_text),
            run_time=1.3
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Swap out-of-order bars", seconds=3)
    def swap_elements(self):
        v1, v2 = self.values[self.idx1], self.values[self.idx2]

        # Target center locations after swap
        target_pos1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx2).get_center()
        target_pos2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx1).get_center()

        path1 = ArcBetweenPoints(self.bars[self.idx1].get_center(), target_pos1, angle=-PI / 2)
        path2 = ArcBetweenPoints(self.bars[self.idx2].get_center(), target_pos2, angle=-PI / 2)

        swapped1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx2, color=GREEN_C)
        swapped2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx1, color=GREEN_C)

        sorted_text = Text(
            f"{v2} < {v1}  (Sorted)",
            font_size=28,
            color=GREEN_C
        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)

        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.bars[self.idx1], path1),
            MoveAlongPath(self.bars[self.idx2], path2),
            Transform(self.cmp_text, sorted_text),
            run_time=1.8
        )

        self.play(
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx1], swapped1),
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx2], swapped2),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(0.4)
```

```python
        figure_eight.set_points_smoothly(points)
        figure_eight.scale(2)  # Make it larger
```

```python
"""Gold scene 002 — learning rate and gradient descent.

The whole scene is driven by ``forge.primitives.optimise.Descent``. Nothing
about any trajectory is authored: the ball goes where the update rule sends it,
the divergence diverges because the arithmetic diverges, and the reported final
positions are read off the run rather than typed in.

That is the property worth training on. A model that learns to draw a plausible
descent curve has learned decoration. A model that learns to *run the optimiser
and animate the result* has learned something true.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.optimise import Descent, minimum_of

CURVE_C = BLUE_C
BALL_C = YELLOW_C
GOOD_C = "#5CD0B3"
BAD_C = "#FC6255"
SLOW_C = "#F0AC5F"

X_LO, X_HI = -5.0, 5.0


def loss(x: float) -> float:
    return 0.35 * x ** 2 + 0.4 * x + 1.2


class LearningRate(ForgeScene):

    x0 = 3.4

    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------------

    def make_axes(self) -> Axes:
        return Axes(
            x_range=[X_LO, X_HI, 1], y_range=[0, 11, 2],
            x_length=7.4, y_length=4.9,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2,
                         "color": GREY_B, "font_size": 20},
        ).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.35)

    def on_curve(self, x: float):
        return self.axes.c2p(x, loss(x))

    def run_descent(self, lr: float, n: int = 14) -> Descent:
        return Descent(loss, x0=self.x0, lr=lr, n_steps=n)

    def panel_text(self, *lines, color=WHITE, size=26) -> VGroup:
        return VGroup(*[Text(l, font_size=size, color=color) for l in lines]) \
            .arrange(DOWN, buff=0.16, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 1.4, 0])

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw the loss curve and mark its true minimum", seconds=5)
    def setup_curve(self):
        self.axes = self.make_axes()
        self.curve = self.axes.plot(loss, x_range=[X_LO, X_HI], color=CURVE_C,
                                    stroke_width=4)
        self.title = Text("Gradient descent", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)

        min_x, min_y = minimum_of(loss, X_LO, X_HI)     # found, not assumed
        self.min_dot = Dot(self.axes.c2p(min_x, min_y), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.07)
        # Below the x-axis, not between dot and axis: the curve's minimum sits
        # close enough to y=0 that a label placed under the dot lands on the
        # tick marks.
        self.min_label = Text("minimum", font_size=20, color=GOOD_C)
        self.min_label.next_to(self.axes.c2p(min_x, 0), DOWN, buff=0.28)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), Create(self.axes), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=1.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.min_dot, scale=0.5), Write(self.min_label), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Place a ball on the slope and show the gradient", seconds=5)
    def show_gradient(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        g = d.steps[0].grad

        self.ball = Dot(self.on_curve(self.x0), color=BALL_C, radius=0.11)
        span = 1.15
        tangent = Line(
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 - span, loss(self.x0) - g * span),
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 + span, loss(self.x0) + g * span),
            color=BALL_C, stroke_width=3,
        )

        self.rule = self.panel_text("the slope tells you", "which way is downhill",
                                    color=GREY_B, size=23)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.ball, scale=0.4), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Create(tangent), FadeIn(self.rule, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(0.6)
        self.play(FadeOut(tangent), FadeOut(self.rule), run_time=0.5)

    @beat("A good learning rate walks the ball to the minimum", seconds=8)
    def good_rate(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.55", color=GOOD_C, size=30)
        self.play(FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.6)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps[:10]:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.045).set_opacity(0.55)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(
                self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.28, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine,
            )

        verdict = Text(f"settles at x = {d.final_x:.2f}", font_size=24, color=GOOD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too large a step and it climbs out of the valley", seconds=8)
    def too_large(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=3.5)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "3.5", color=BAD_C, size=30)

        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        # Only the steps still inside the frame can be drawn; the rest is the point.
        visible = [s for s in d.steps if X_LO < s.next_x < X_HI][:6]
        for s in visible:
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      run_time=0.32, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine)

        arrow = Arrow(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 1.4, 8.2), self.axes.c2p(X_HI, 10.4),
                      color=BAD_C, buff=0, stroke_width=5)
        gone = Text("off the chart", font_size=22, color=BAD_C).next_to(arrow, LEFT, buff=0.12)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 0.2, 10.0)).set_opacity(0.3),
                  GrowArrow(arrow), FadeIn(gone), run_time=0.9)

        verdict = Text(f"reaches x = {d.final_x:,.0f}", font_size=24, color=BAD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(gone), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict),
                  self.ball.animate.set_opacity(1.0), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too small and it never arrives", seconds=7)
    def too_small(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.15)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.15", color=SLOW_C, size=30)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=SLOW_C, radius=0.04).set_opacity(0.5)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.2)

        verdict = Text(f"only x = {d.final_x:.2f} after {len(d.steps)} steps",
                       font_size=22, color=SLOW_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("The three rates side by side", seconds=6)
    def compare(self):
        rows = VGroup()
        for lr, colour, note in ((0.15, SLOW_C, "too small"),
                                 (0.55, GOOD_C, "about right"),
                                 (3.5, BAD_C, "too large")):
            d = self.run_descent(lr)
            rows.add(VGroup(
                Text(f"{lr}", font_size=26, color=colour),
                Text(note, font_size=20, color=GREY_B),
            ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN))
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.34, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=RIGHT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.25, run_time=1.6))
        self.play(Indicate(rows[1], color=GOOD_C, scale_factor=1.12), run_time=0.9)
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
    def create_pendulum(self):

        bob = Dot()
        bob.move_to(DOWN * 2)
        line = Line(pivot.get_center(), bob.get_center())
        return VGroup(pivot, line, bob)

        orbit = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE)
        orbit.move_to(axes.get_center())
        return VGroup(axes, orbit)
    
    def create_poincare_map(self):
        # Poincaré map dots
        dots = VGroup()
        for i in range(12):
            angle = i * 2 * PI / 12
            radius = 1.5
            x = radius * np.cos(angle)
            y = radius * np.sin(angle)
            dot = Dot(point=[x, y, 0], radius=0.1, color=RED)

        return dots
```

```python
    def setup_axes(self):
        self.axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 50, 10],
            y_range=[0, 14, 2],
            x_length=8.5,
            y_length=6.5,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": True, "font_size": 24}
        ).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)
        
        self.x_label = Text("Volume of Base Added (mL)", font_size=20).next_to(self.axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.4).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)
        self.y_label = Text("pH", font_size=20).next_to(self.axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(self.axes), Write(self.x_label), Write(self.y_label), run_time=3.0)

    @beat("Show the initial low pH state", seconds=4, narration="We start with a strong acid in the flask. The pH is very low, around 1.")
    def initial_state(self):
        # Compute exact starting point for V = 0
        start_point = self.xy_to_screen(0, 1.0)
        self.dot = Dot(point=start_point, color=BLUE_C, radius=0.1)
        
        self.ph_label = DecimalNumber(1.0, num_decimal_places=1, font_size=32, color=BLUE_C)
        self.ph_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(self.dot, UP + RIGHT, buff=0.2))
        self.ph_label.set_value(1.0)
        
        flask_text = Text("Strong Acid\n(pH ~ 1.0)", font_size=20, color=BLUE_C).to_edge(UP).to_edge(LEFT)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(flask_text, shift=DOWN), FadeIn(self.dot, scale=0.5), Write(self.ph_label), run_time=3.0)

    @beat("Add base slowly in the buffer region", seconds=5, narration="As we add base, the pH rises very slowly because excess unreacted acid buffers the solution.")
    def buffer_region(self):
        target_point = self.xy_to_screen(20, 2.3)
        curve_segment = Line(self.dot.get_center(), target_point, color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.dot, curve_segment),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(self.ph_label, 2.3),
            run_time=4.0
        )
        self.saved_curve_part1 = curve_segment

    @beat("Highlight the half-equivalence point", seconds=5, narration="At the half-equivalence point, exactly half the acid has been neutralized, and pH equals pKa.")
    def half_equivalence(self):
        v_half = 25.0
        ph_half = 7.0
        target_point = self.xy_to_screen(v_half, ph_half)
        
        curve_segment = Line(self.dot.get_center(), target_point, color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=4)
        
        dash_x = DashedLine(self.axes.c2p(v_half, 0), target_point, dash_length=0.1, color=GRAY)
        dash_y = DashedLine(self.axes.c2p(0, ph_half), target_point, dash_length=0.1, color=GRAY)
        
        note = Text("Equivalence Point (pH 7.0)", font_size=22, color=GREEN_C).to_edge(UP).to_edge(LEFT)
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.dot, curve_segment),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(self.ph_label, 7.0),
            Create(dash_x),
            Create(dash_y),
            run_time=4.0
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=DOWN), run_time=1.0)

    @beat("Show the sharp vertical spike", seconds=5, narration="Then comes the equivalence point. A tiny drop of base causes the pH to shoot straight up vertically.")
    def vertical_spike(self):
        target_point = self.xy_to_screen(25.5, 12.0)
        curve_segment = Line(self.dot.get_center(), target_point, color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.dot, curve_segment),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(self.ph_label, 12.0),
            run_time=4.0
        )

    @beat("Level off in the basic region", seconds=5, narration="Finally, excess base dominates, and the curve flattens out at a very high pH.")
    def final_region(self):
        target_point = self.xy_to_screen(50, 13.5)
        curve_segment = Line(self.dot.get_center(), target_point, color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.dot, curve_segment),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(self.ph_label, 13.5),
            run_time=4.0
        )

    @beat("Clean up and display the full titration curve", seconds=5, narration="Putting it all together, we get this classic sigmoidal titration curve.")
    def show_full_curve(self):
        # Generate full smooth curve mathematically to replace linear segments
        def curve_func(x):
            # Sigmoid approximation for titration
            # x goes 0 to 50
            normalized = (x - 25.0) / 4.0
            import math
            # logistic-like shift
            val = 1.0 + 12.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-normalized))
            return val

        full_curve = self.axes.plot(curve_func, x_range=[0, 50], color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(self.dot),
            FadeOut(self.ph_label),
            Transform(self.axes, self.axes),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        
        complete_label = Text("Titration Curve", font_size=28, color=YELLOW_D).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Create(full_curve), Write(complete_label), run_time=3.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
```

```python
from manim import *

class WilsonsTheoremScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Set background color
        self.camera.background_color = "#0A1A2A"
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Wilson's Theorem Unveiled", color=GOLD)
        subtitle = Text("Looping Through Primes on the Circle", color=GOLD).scale(0.7)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Write(subtitle))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Wilson's Theorem statement
        theorem = Text("Wilson's Theorem:", color=GOLD)
        formula = Text("(p-1)! + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p) for p prime", color=WHITE)
        formula.next_to(theorem, DOWN)
        
        theorem_group = VGroup(theorem, formula)
        
        self.play(Write(theorem_group))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(theorem_group.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Create a unit circle for modular arithmetic
        p = 5  # Using p = 5 for visualization
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color=GOLD)
        
        self.play(Create(circle))
        
        # Label for modulo
        mod_label = Text(f"Modulo {p}", color=GOLD).scale(0.7)
        mod_label.next_to(circle, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(Write(mod_label))
        
        # Create points for each residue class
        dots = VGroup()
        labels = VGroup()
        
        for i in range(p):
            angle = i * 2 * PI / p
            point = circle.point_at_angle(angle)
            dot = Dot(point, color=WHITE)
            label = Text(str(i), color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
            label.next_to(dot, direction=point/2, buff=0.1)
            
            dots.add(dot)
            labels.add(label)
        
        self.play(Create(dots))
        self.play(Write(labels))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Explanation text
        explanation = Text("For p=5, calculating (p-1)! = 4!", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        explanation.next_to(mod_label, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(Write(explanation))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Start with 1
        product = 1
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=dots[1].get_center(), color=RED)  # Start at 1
        calc_text = Text(f"Starting with: {product}", color=RED).scale(0.7)
        calc_text.next_to(explanation, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(calc_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Calculate factorial
        for i in range(1, p):
            old_product = product
```

```python
class GraphPlanarityScene(Scene):

        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Create a simplified graph with 4 nodes
        node1 = Dot([-1.5, 1, 0], color=BLUE)
        node2 = Dot([1.5, 1, 0], color=BLUE)
        node3 = Dot([1.5, -1, 0], color=BLUE)
        node4 = Dot([-1.5, -1, 0], color=BLUE)
        
        # Add labels to nodes
        label1 = Text("A", font_size=20).next_to(node1, UP)
        label2 = Text("B", font_size=20).next_to(node2, UP)
        label3 = Text("C", font_size=20).next_to(node3, DOWN)
        label4 = Text("D", font_size=20).next_to(node4, DOWN)
        
        # Create edges
        edge1 = Line(node1.get_center(), node2.get_center(), color=WHITE)  # A-B
        edge2 = Line(node2.get_center(), node3.get_center(), color=WHITE)  # B-C
        edge3 = Line(node3.get_center(), node4.get_center(), color=WHITE)  # C-D
        edge4 = Line(node4.get_center(), node1.get_center(), color=WHITE)  # D-A
        edge5 = Line(node1.get_center(), node3.get_center(), color=RED)    # A-C (crossing)
        edge6 = Line(node2.get_center(), node4.get_center(), color=RED)    # B-D (crossing)
        
        # Display graph elements
        self.play(
            Create(node1), Create(node2), Create(node3), Create(node4),
            Write(label1), Write(label2), Write(label3), Write(label4)
        )
        self.play(
            Create(edge1), Create(edge2), Create(edge3), Create(edge4)
        )
        self.play(Create(edge5), Create(edge6))
        
        # Show text about non-planarity
        non_planar_text = Text("Non-planar graph: red edges cross", font_size=20)
        non_planar_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=1)
        self.play(Write(non_planar_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight edge to contract
        self.play(edge1.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        contract_text = Text("Let's contract this edge", font_size=20)
        contract_text.next_to(non_planar_text, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(contract_text))
        self.wait(1)

        midpoint = (node1.get_center() + node2.get_center()) / 2
        merged_node = Dot(midpoint, color=GREEN, radius=0.15)
        merged_label = Text("AB", font_size=20).next_to(merged_node, UP)
        
        # Animation for contraction
        self.play(
            node1.animate.move_to(midpoint),
            node2.animate.move_to(midpoint),
            FadeOut(label1),
            FadeOut(label2)
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(node1),
            FadeOut(node2),
            FadeOut(edge1),
            Create(merged_node),
            Write(merged_label)
        )
        
        # Update the graph
        new_edge1 = Line(merged_node.get_center(), node3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        new_edge2 = Line(merged_node.get_center(), node4.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(edge2),
            FadeOut(edge4),
            FadeOut(edge5),
            FadeOut(edge6),
            Create(new_edge1),
            Create(new_edge2)
        )
        
        # Final result
        self.play(FadeOut(contract_text))
        result_text = Text("Result: A planar graph (no crossing edges)", font_size=20)
        result_text.next_to(non_planar_text, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(result_text))

        # Fade out everything
```

```python
"""Gold scene 001 — rook mobility and corner probability.

Authored by hand from Nimit's own prompt:

    "build me a chess grid, add rooks on it and animate the rook's possible
     movements, then help me calculate the probability that if i place the
     rook at any square, it is a corner square"

This is a *target*, not a sample: the standard the fine-tuned model has to
reach. Two properties make it gold rather than merely working.

**Every number on screen is computed.** The 4, the 64 and the 1/16 come from
counting cells in ``forge.primitives.grid``. Nothing here recites a figure a
language model happened to remember.

**It answers more than it was asked.** The prompt requested rook movement and
corner probability as two separate things. Beat 4 finds the link worth showing:
a rook reaches exactly 14 squares from *every* square on the board, corners
included. That invariance came out of writing the primitive, and it is the
difference between a diagram and an explanation.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.grid import Board, Cell

# A restrained palette: neutral board, one colour for attention, one for the
# result. Loud boards fight the thing you are trying to point at.
LIGHT_SQ = "#3D4852"
DARK_SQ = "#2A313A"
ROOK_C = BLUE_C
REACH_C = YELLOW_C
CORNER_C = "#5CD0B3"

CELL = 0.70
BOARD_X = -3.1      # board centre; right half is the information panel
PANEL_X = 3.4


def rook_glyph(color=ROOK_C) -> VGroup:
    """A rook built from primitives rather than a font glyph — no typeface to
    be missing, and it scales cleanly."""
    base = Rectangle(width=0.40, height=0.07, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem = Rectangle(width=0.24, height=0.24, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    head = Rectangle(width=0.36, height=0.10, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem.next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
    head.next_to(stem, UP, buff=0)
    return VGroup(base, stem, head)


class RookCorners(ForgeScene):

    board = Board(8, 8)

    # -- geometry helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def xy(self, cell: Cell) -> np.ndarray:
        """Cell -> world coordinates, with the board centred on the origin."""
        x = BOARD_X + (cell.col - (self.board.cols - 1) / 2) * CELL
        y = (cell.row - (self.board.rows - 1) / 2) * CELL - 0.3
        return np.array([x, y, 0.0])

    def tile(self, cell: Cell, color, opacity=0.85) -> Square:
        return Square(side_length=CELL, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=color, fill_opacity=opacity).move_to(self.xy(cell))

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw an 8x8 chessboard", seconds=3)
    def draw_board(self):
        self.squares = VGroup(*[
            self.tile(c, LIGHT_SQ if self.board.is_light(c) else DARK_SQ, 1.0)
            for c in self.board.cells()
        ])
        self.title = Text("A rook on an 8 x 8 board", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s, scale=0.6) for s in self.squares],
                              lag_ratio=0.012, run_time=2.0))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)

    @beat("Place a rook on d4", seconds=2)
    def place_rook(self):
        self.origin = Cell(3, 3)                      # d4
        self.rook = rook_glyph().move_to(self.xy(self.origin))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.rook, shift=UP * 0.4), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(self.rook, color=ROOK_C, line_length=0.16, num_lines=10,
                        flash_radius=0.42), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight every square the rook can reach", seconds=5)
    def show_reach(self):
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(self.origin)     # computed, not hardcoded
        self.reach_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.count = VGroup(
            Text(str(len(reach)), font_size=72, color=REACH_C),
            Text("reachable squares", font_size=24, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.18).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t) for t in self.reach_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.05, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.count[0], scale=0.7), Write(self.count[1]), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.4)

    @beat("Move the rook to the corner - the count is unchanged", seconds=5)
    def corner_is_no_different(self):
        corner = Cell(0, 0)                            # a1
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(corner)
        new_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.play(
            self.rook.animate.move_to(self.xy(corner)),
            Transform(self.reach_tiles, new_tiles),
            run_time=1.6,
        )
        # The count is unchanged, so the numeral must visibly hold still while
        # everything around it moves — that stillness *is* the point of the beat.
        self.play(Indicate(self.count[0], color=REACH_C, scale_factor=1.25), run_time=0.8)

        note = VGroup(
            Text("still 14.", font_size=28, color=REACH_C),
            Text("a rook's reach is the", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
            Text("same from every square", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.12).move_to([PANEL_X, -1.5, 0])
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.9)
        self.play(FadeOut(note), FadeOut(self.reach_tiles), FadeOut(self.count),
                  run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight the four corner squares", seconds=4)
    def show_corners(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()                 # computed -> 4
        self.corner_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, CORNER_C, 0.55) for c in corners])

        new_title = Text("How likely is a corner?", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(Transform(self.title, new_title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rook, shift=DOWN * 0.3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(t) for t in self.corner_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.4))
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Derive the probability as an exact fraction", seconds=6)
    def derive(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()
        p = self.board.probability_of(corners)         # Fraction(1, 16) - exact

        expr = MathTex(
            r"P(\text{corner})", "=",
            rf"\frac{{{len(corners)}}}{{{self.board.n_cells}}}",
            font_size=42,
        ).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])
        expr[2].set_color(CORNER_C)

        reduced = MathTex("=", rf"\frac{{{p.numerator}}}{{{p.denominator}}}", font_size=52)
        reduced[1].set_color(CORNER_C)
        reduced.next_to(expr, DOWN, buff=0.45)

        self.play(Write(expr[0]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Write(expr[1]), Write(expr[2]), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(reduced), run_time=0.9)

        pct = Text(f"{float(p) * 100:.2f}%", font_size=26, color=GREY_B)
        pct.next_to(reduced, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(pct, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.6)
        self.expr, self.reduced, self.pct = expr, reduced, pct
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat

class CollatzBouncer(ForgeScene):
    @beat("Introduce the Collatz rule: even halves, odd triples-plus-one", seconds=3)
    def introduce_rule(self):
        title = Text("The Collatz Conjecture", font_size=40, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        rule_even = MathTex(r"n \rightarrow \frac{n}{2}", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
        rule_odd = MathTex(r"n \rightarrow 3n + 1", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        
        rules = VGroup(
            Text("If even:", font_size=30), rule_even,
            Text("If odd:", font_size=30), rule_odd
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).shift(LEFT * 3)

        self.play(Write(title), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(rules, shift=RIGHT), run_time=2)

    @beat("Trace the sequence from 6 down to 1", seconds=3)
    def trace_sequence(self):
        # Compute Collatz sequence for 6 step-by-step
        n = 6
        seq = [n]
        while n > 1:
            if n % 2 == 0:
                n = n // 2
            else:
                n = 3 * n + 1
            seq.append(n)

        # seq will be [6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1]
        seq_tex = MathTex(
            r" \rightarrow ".join(str(x) for x in seq),
            font_size=36
        ).shift(RIGHT * 1.5)

        note = Text(f"Length: {len(seq)} steps", font_size=28, color=GRAY).next_to(seq_tex, DOWN, buff=0.8)

        self.play(Write(seq_tex), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP), run_time=1)
```

```python
        # Basic payoff grid (without fairness)

        # Create a gradient pattern for basic payoffs
        for i in range(grid_size):
            for j in range(grid_size):
                # Calculate a simple gradient value
                value = (i + j) / (2 * grid_size - 2)  # Normalize to 0-1
                
                square = Square(side_length=square_size)
                square.set_fill(color=interpolate_color(BLUE, RED, value), opacity=0.7)
                square.move_to([

                    start_y - i * square_size,
                    0

                payoff_grid.add(square)

        payoff_eq = MathTex(r"\text{Payoff Function: } U_i = f(s_i, s_{-i})")
        payoff_eq.next_to(explanation1, DOWN)
```
