```python
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Create a new grid with fairness adjustments
        fairness_grid = VGroup()
        
        # More balanced distribution to represent fairness
        for i in range(grid_size):
            for j in range(grid_size):
                # Base value
                base_value = (i + j) / (2 * grid_size - 2)
                # Fairness adjustment - makes distribution more even
                fairness_factor = 0.5 - abs(base_value - 0.5)
                adjusted_value = base_value + 0.3 * fairness_factor
                
                # Clamp between 0 and 1
                adjusted_value = max(0, min(1, adjusted_value))
                
                square = Square(side_length=square_size)
                square.set_fill(color=interpolate_color(BLUE, RED, adjusted_value), opacity=0.7)
                square.move_to([
                    start_x + j * square_size,
                    start_y - i * square_size,
                    0
                ])
                fairness_grid.add(square)
        
        # Explanation for fairness adjustment
        explanation2 = Text("Payoff distribution with fairness adjustments", font_size=24)
        explanation2.next_to(payoff_grid, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # Equation for fairness

            ReplacementTransform(payoff_grid, fairness_grid),
            ReplacementTransform(explanation1, explanation2),
            ReplacementTransform(payoff_eq, fairness_eq)

        # Highlight a region of interest
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.8, color=YELLOW)

        # Pulsing effect to draw attention

        )

        self.play(FadeOut(conclusion))
```

```python
import numpy as np
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat


class CrossProductArea(ForgeScene):
    origin = np.array([-4.5, -1.5, 0.0])
    vec_a = np.array([3.2, 0.0, 0.0])
    vec_b = np.array([1.4, 2.6, 0.0])

    @beat("Introduce vectors a and b", seconds=4)
    def introduce_vectors(self):
        self.arrow_a = Arrow(
            self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_a, buff=0, color=BLUE_C
        )
        self.arrow_b = Arrow(
            self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_b, buff=0, color=YELLOW_C
        )

        self.label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{a}", color=BLUE_C).next_to(
            self.arrow_a, DOWN, buff=0.15
        )
        self.label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{b}", color=YELLOW_C).next_to(
            self.arrow_b.get_center(), UL, buff=0.15
        )

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(self.arrow_a),
            Write(self.label_a),
            GrowArrow(self.arrow_b),
            Write(self.label_b),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Construct the spanned parallelogram", seconds=4)
    def construct_parallelogram(self):
        p0 = self.origin
        p1 = self.origin + self.vec_a
        p2 = self.origin + self.vec_a + self.vec_b
        p3 = self.origin + self.vec_b

        self.parallelogram = Polygon(
            p0, p1, p2, p3,
            fill_color=TEAL_E,
            fill_opacity=0.45,
            stroke_color=TEAL_B,
            stroke_width=2,
        )

        edge_top = DashedLine(p3, p2, color=BLUE_C)
        edge_right = DashedLine(p1, p2, color=YELLOW_C)

        self.play(
            Create(edge_top),
            Create(edge_right),
            FadeIn(self.parallelogram),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Deconstruct geometric height and angle", seconds=4)
    def show_height_and_angle(self):
        p_drop = np.array([self.origin[0] + self.vec_b[0], self.origin[1], 0.0])
        p_top = self.origin + self.vec_b

        self.height_line = DashedLine(p_top, p_drop, color=RED_C, stroke_width=3)
        self.height_label = MathTex(
            r"h = \|\vec{b}\|\sin\theta", font_size=28, color=RED_C
        ).next_to(self.height_line, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        line_a = Line(self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_a)
        line_b = Line(self.origin, self.origin + self.vec_b)
        self.angle_arc = Angle(line_a, line_b, radius=0.65, color=WHITE)
        self.theta_label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=26).next_to(
            self.angle_arc, UR, buff=0.05
        )

        self.play(
            Create(self.angle_arc),
            Write(self.theta_label),
            Create(self.height_line),
            Write(self.height_label),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Derive the cross product magnitude formula", seconds=4)
    def derive_formula(self):
        title = Text("Parallelogram Area", font_size=32, color=WHITE).move_to(
            [3.2, 2.2, 0]
        )
        eq1 = MathTex(r"\text{Area} = \text{base} \times \text{height}", font_size=30)
        eq2 = MathTex(r"= \|\vec{a}\| \cdot (\|\vec{b}\|\sin\theta)", font_size=30)
        eq3 = MathTex(r"= \|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\|", font_size=34, color=YELLOW_C)

        formula_group = (
            VGroup(title, eq1, eq2, eq3)
            .arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.35)
            .move_to([3.2, 0.8, 0])
        )

        self.play(Write(title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq1), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq2), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq3), run_time=1.0)
        self.formula_group = formula_group

    @beat("Compute the numerical area dynamically", seconds=4)
    def compute_numerical_area(self):
        # Compute exact values programmatically from vector coordinates
        cross_vector = np.cross(self.vec_a, self.vec_b)
        area_val = np.linalg.norm(cross_vector)
        norm_a_val = np.linalg.norm(self.vec_a)
        norm_b_val = np.linalg.norm(self.vec_b)

        calc_box = RoundedRectangle(
            corner_radius=0.15,
            width=4.6,
            height=1.8,
            color=GRAY_B,
            fill_color=DARK_GRAY,
            fill_opacity=0.3,
        ).move_to([3.2, -2.0, 0])

        calc_label = VGroup(
            MathTex(
                rf"\|\vec{{a}}\| = {norm_a_val:.1f},\quad \|\vec{{b}}\| \approx {norm_b_val:.2f}",
                font_size=24,
            ),
            MathTex(
                rf"\text{{Computed Area}} = {area_val:.2f}",
                font_size=30,
                color=GREEN_C,
            ),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25).move_to(calc_box)

        self.play(
            Create(calc_box),
            Write(calc_label),
            self.parallelogram.animate.set_fill(GREEN_D, opacity=0.55),
            run_time=2.5,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
```

```python
            np.array([-1.4, 0, 0]),

        ]
```

```python
import numpy as np

class LawOfLargeNumbersScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define colors for the three distributions
        uniform_color = "#1E8449"  # Green
        normal_color = "#2E86C1"   # Blue
        exponential_color = "#C0392B"  # Red
        
        # Create and display title
        title = Text("Visualizing Convergence: The Law of Large Numbers", font_size=32)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Simple coin flip animation to introduce randomness concept
        coin = Circle(radius=1, color=WHITE).set_fill(GOLD, opacity=0.8)
        coin_text = Text("H", font_size=40).move_to(coin.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(coin), Write(coin_text))
        self.play(
            Rotate(coin, angle=PI),
            Transform(coin_text, Text("T", font_size=40).move_to(coin.get_center()))
        )
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(coin), FadeOut(coin_text))
        
        # Create a coordinate system for plotting convergence paths
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 100, 20],
            y_range=[0, 10, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.75)
        
        x_label = Text("Number of Samples", font_size=20).next_to(axes, DOWN)
        y_label = Text("Sample Mean", font_size=20).next_to(axes, LEFT).rotate(PI/2)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        
        # Define theoretical means for each distribution
        uniform_mean = 5
        normal_mean = 5
        exp_mean = 2
        
        # Create horizontal lines representing the theoretical means
        uniform_line = DashedLine(
            start=axes.c2p(0, uniform_mean),
            end=axes.c2p(100, uniform_mean),
            color=uniform_color
        )
        
        normal_line = DashedLine(
            start=axes.c2p(0, normal_mean),
            end=axes.c2p(100, normal_mean),
            color=normal_color
        )
        
        exp_line = DashedLine(
            start=axes.c2p(0, exp_mean),
            end=axes.c2p(100, exp_mean),
            color=exponential_color
        )
        
        # Add labels for each distribution
        uniform_label = Text("Uniform", color=uniform_color, font_size=20).next_to(uniform_line, RIGHT)
        normal_label = Text("Normal", color=normal_color, font_size=20).next_to(normal_line, RIGHT)
        exp_label = Text("Exponential", color=exponential_color, font_size=20).next_to(exp_line, RIGHT)
        
        # Show the mean lines and labels
        self.play(
            Create(uniform_line), Write(uniform_label),
            Create(normal_line), Write(normal_label),
            Create(exp_line), Write(exp_label)
        )
        
        # Display the population mean equations
        equations = VGroup(
            Text("μ = (a+b)/2", color=uniform_color, font_size=24),
            Text("μ = μx", color=normal_color, font_size=24),
            Text("μ = 1/λ", color=exponential_color, font_size=24)
        ).arrange(DOWN).to_edge(RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Write(equations))
        
        # Function to generate points that converge to the mean
        np.random.seed(42)  # For reproducibility
        
        def generate_points(mean, std_dev, num_points=10):
            points = []
            
            for i in range(num_points+1):
                x = i * 10  # Spread points along x-axis
                
                # The closer to the end, the closer to the mean
                if i == 0:
                    y = np.random.uniform(1, 9)  # Start random
                else:
                    # Gradually converge to mean
                    variation = std_dev * (1 - i/num_points)**2
                    y = mean + np.random.normal(0, variation)
                
                points.append((x, y))
            
            return points
        
        # Generate convergence paths for each distribution
        uniform_points = generate_points(uniform_mean, 1.5)
        normal_points = generate_points(normal_mean, 1.0)
        exp_points = generate_points(exp_mean, 2.0)
        
        # Create visual path objects
        uniform_path = VMobject(color=uniform_color)
        uniform_path.set_points_as_corners([axes.c2p(x, y) for x, y in uniform_points])
        
        normal_path = VMobject(color=normal_color)
        normal_path.set_points_as_corners([axes.c2p(x, y) for x, y in normal_points])
        
        exp_path = VMobject(color=exponential_color)
        exp_path.set_points_as_corners([axes.c2p(x, y) for x, y in exp_points])
        
        # Animate the paths one by one
        self.play(Create(uniform_path), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(normal_path), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(exp_path), run_time=2)
        
        # Show conclusion
        conclusion = Text("As samples increase, means converge to theoretical values", font_size=24)
        conclusion.next_to(axes, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final message after clearing everything
        final_message = Text("The Law of Large Numbers!", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(uniform_path), FadeOut(normal_path), 
            FadeOut(exp_path), FadeOut(uniform_line), FadeOut(normal_line), 
            FadeOut(exp_line), FadeOut(uniform_label), FadeOut(normal_label), 
            FadeOut(exp_label), FadeOut(equations), FadeOut(x_label), 
            FadeOut(y_label), FadeOut(conclusion), FadeOut(title)
        )
        
        self.play(Write(final_message))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
        colors = [
            "#f55e61",
            "#5fcb50",
            "#408ef5",
            "#e3883d",
            "#a346eb",
            "#0dc786",
            "#34a853",
            "#bf2626",
            "#3333FF",
            "#b3a77d",
            "#b85842"
        ]
        
        fib_numbers = [0, 1]
        for _ in range(7):
            fib_numbers.append(fib_numbers[-1] + fib_numbers[-2])

        squares = VGroup()
        for index, fib_num in enumerate(fib_numbers[2:]):
            square = Square(
                side_length=fib_num,
                color=colors[index % len(colors)],
                fill_opacity=0.5
            )
            squares.add(square)
        
        spirals = VGroup()
        start_point = ORIGIN
        angle = 0
        for index, square in enumerate(squares):
            square.move_to(start_point)
            spirals.add(Arc(
                start_angle=angle,
                angle=TAU/4,
                radius=square.side_length/2,
                color=colors[index % len(colors)]
            ).move_arc_center_to(start_point))
            if index % 4 == 0:
                start_point += square.side_length * RIGHT / 2
                start_point += squares[index - 1].side_length * UP / 2 if index > 0 else ORIGIN
                angle += TAU / 4
            elif index % 4 == 1:
                start_point += square.side_length * UP / 2
                start_point += squares[index - 1].side_length * LEFT / 2
                angle += TAU / 4
            elif index % 4 == 2:
                start_point += square.side_length * LEFT / 2
                start_point += squares[index - 1].side_length * DOWN / 2
                angle += TAU / 4
            else:
                start_point += square.side_length * DOWN / 2
                start_point += squares[index - 1].side_length * RIGHT / 2
                angle += TAU / 4

        fibonacci_spiral = VGroup(squares, spirals).move_to(ORIGIN)
        self.play(Create(fibonacci_spiral), run_time=4)
        self.wait()
```

```python
import numpy as np

class MonteCarloPI(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Create the title
        title = Text("Dancing with Randomness: Estimating π with Monte Carlo")
        title.set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Create the square and circle
        square = Square(side_length=4, color=BLUE_C).shift(LEFT * 2.5)
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color=GREEN_C).shift(LEFT * 2.5)
        
        self.play(Create(square), Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Initialize counters
        points_inside = 0
        total_points = 0
        
        # Display counters
        inside_text = Text(f"Points inside: {points_inside}", font_size=24, color=GREEN_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1.5)
        total_text = Text(f"Total points: {total_points}", font_size=24, color=BLUE_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1)
        pi_estimate_text = Text(f"π estimate: 0", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(inside_text), Write(total_text), Write(pi_estimate_text))
        
        # Generate random points
        num_points = 30  # For a shorter animation
        
        for i in range(num_points):
            # Generate a random point within the square
            x = np.random.uniform(-2, 2)
            y = np.random.uniform(-2, 2)
            
            # Check if the point is inside the circle
            inside_circle = x**2 + y**2 <= 4  # Circle has radius 2
            
            if inside_circle:
                points_inside += 1
                point_color = GREEN_C
            else:
                point_color = ORANGE
            
            total_points += 1
            
            # Create a point at the random location
            point = Dot(point=np.array([x, y, 0]) + LEFT * 2.5, color=point_color)
            
            # Update the counters
            new_inside_text = Text(f"Points inside: {points_inside}", font_size=24, color=GREEN_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1.5)
            new_total_text = Text(f"Total points: {total_points}", font_size=24, color=BLUE_C).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 1)
            pi_estimate = 4 * points_inside / total_points
            new_pi_estimate_text = Text(f"π estimate: {pi_estimate:.4f}", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + UP * 0.5)
            
            # Animate the addition of the point and update the counters
            self.play(
                Create(point),
                Transform(inside_text, new_inside_text),
                Transform(total_text, new_total_text),
                Transform(pi_estimate_text, new_pi_estimate_text),
                run_time=0.1  # Fast animation
            )
        
        # Show the actual value of pi
        actual_pi = Text(f"Actual π: {np.pi:.4f}", font_size=24, color=ORANGE).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 1)
        self.play(Write(actual_pi))
        
        # Conclude with the formula
        formula = Text("Estimated π = 4 × (Inside Points / Total Points)", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        formula.scale(0.7).to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
from manim import *

class AdaptiveQuadratureScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Adapting to Discontinuity: The Magic of Adaptive Quadrature", font_size=32)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.scale(0.7).to_edge(UP))
        
        # Create axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"color": BLUE}
        )
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        # Create a discontinuous function
        def f(x):
            if abs(x) < 0.1:  # Avoid division by zero
                return 0
            elif x < 0:
                return -1/x if x > -2 else 1
            else:
                return 1/x if x < 2 else 1
            
        # Plot the function
        left_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: f(x), x_range=[-3, -0.1], color=RED)
        right_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: f(x), x_range=[0.1, 3], color=RED)
        
        function_label = MathTex(r"f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{x}, & x \neq 0 \\ 0, & x = 0 \end{cases}")
        function_label.scale(0.7).next_to(axes, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(left_curve), Create(right_curve), Write(function_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight the discontinuity
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Regular quadrature - uniform intervals
        regular_rects = VGroup()
        step = 0.5
        
        for x in np.arange(-2.75, 2.8, step):
            if -0.25 < x < 0.25:  # Skip near discontinuity
                continue
            
            height = f(x)
            if abs(height) > 3:  # Cap very tall rectangles 
                height = 3 * (1 if height > 0 else -1)
                
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=step,
                height=abs(height),
                stroke_width=1,
                fill_color=BLUE,
                fill_opacity=0.5
            )
            
            y_pos = height/2 if height > 0 else height/2
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y_pos))
            regular_rects.add(rect)
        
        regular_text = Text("Regular Quadrature", font_size=20).next_to(function_label, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(regular_text))
        self.play(Create(regular_rects))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Adaptive quadrature - variable intervals
        adaptive_rects = VGroup()
        
        # Wider steps for smooth regions
        wide_step = 0.5
        for x in np.arange(-2.75, -1.0, wide_step):
            height = f(x)
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=wide_step,
                height=abs(height),
                stroke_width=1,
                fill_color=GREEN,
                fill_opacity=0.5
            )
            y_pos = height/2 if height > 0 else height/2
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y_pos))
            adaptive_rects.add(rect)
            
        for x in np.arange(1.0, 2.8, wide_step):
            height = f(x)
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=wide_step,
                height=abs(height),
                stroke_width=1,
                fill_color=GREEN,
                fill_opacity=0.5
            )
            y_pos = height/2 if height > 0 else height/2
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y_pos))
            adaptive_rects.add(rect)
        
        # Finer steps near discontinuity
        fine_step = 0.1
        for x in np.arange(-1.0, -0.1, fine_step):
            height = f(x)
            if abs(height) > 3:
                height = 3 * (1 if height > 0 else -1)
                
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=fine_step,
                height=abs(height),
                stroke_width=1,
                fill_color=YELLOW,
                fill_opacity=0.7
            )
            y_pos = height/2 if height > 0 else height/2
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y_pos))
            adaptive_rects.add(rect)
            
        for x in np.arange(0.1, 1.0, fine_step):
            height = f(x)
            if abs(height) > 3:
                height = 3 * (1 if height > 0 else -1)
                
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=fine_step,
                height=abs(height),
                stroke_width=1,
                fill_color=YELLOW,
                fill_opacity=0.7
            )
            y_pos = height/2 if height > 0 else height/2
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y_pos))
            adaptive_rects.add(rect)
        
        adaptive_text = Text("Adaptive Quadrature", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(function_label, DOWN)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(regular_text, adaptive_text))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(regular_rects, adaptive_rects))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x) \, dx \approx \sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i f(x_i)")
        formula.scale(0.7).next_to(adaptive_text, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Key insight
        insight_text = Text("Smaller steps near discontinuities", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        insight_text.next_to(formula, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(insight_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion = Text("Adaptive quadrature accurately integrates discontinuous functions", font_size=24)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(adaptive_rects),
            FadeOut(highlight),
            FadeOut(left_curve),
            FadeOut(right_curve),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(function_label),
            FadeOut(adaptive_text),
            FadeOut(formula),
            FadeOut(insight_text),
            FadeOut(title),
            Write(conclusion)
        )
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
        # Create fermions as circles
        fermions = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8) for _ in range(6)])
        for i, fermion in enumerate(fermions):
            row = i % 3
            col = i // 3
            fermion.move_to(energy_levels[row].get_center() + RIGHT*(col*2-1))
        
        fermion_label = Text("Fermions", color=RED).scale(0.6).next_to(fermions, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(energy_levels), Write(energy_label))
        self.play(Create(fermions), Write(fermion_label))

        # Clear screen for next section
        self.play(FadeOut(energy_levels), FadeOut(energy_label), 
                  FadeOut(fermions), FadeOut(fermion_label))
        
        # Element 2: Display Fermi-Dirac formula - using Text instead of MathTex for simplicity
        formula = Text("f(E) = 1/(e^((E-μ)/kT) + 1)", color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move formula to top left
        self.play(formula.animate.to_corner(UL))

        axes = Axes(

        x_label = Text("Energy (E)", color=BLUE).scale(0.4).next_to(axes, DOWN)
        y_label = Text("Occupancy (f(E))", color=BLUE).scale(0.4).next_to(axes, LEFT)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        
        # Element 3: Create distribution curves with different temperatures
        def create_fd_curve(temp, color):
            points = []
            for x in np.linspace(0, 5, 50):
                # Simplified Fermi-Dirac distribution
                if temp > 0:
                    y = 1 / (np.exp((x-2.5)/(0.5*temp)) + 1)
                else:
                    y = 1 if x < 2.5 else 0
                points.append(axes.c2p(x, y))
            
            curve = VMobject()
            curve.set_points_as_corners(points)
            curve.set_color(color)
            return curve
        
        # Moderate temperature curve (T=1.0)
        moderate_curve = create_fd_curve(1.0, YELLOW)
        temp_label = Text("T = 1.0", color=YELLOW).scale(0.5).to_corner(UR)
        
        self.play(Create(moderate_curve), Write(temp_label))

        low_curve = create_fd_curve(0.1, BLUE)
        low_temp_label = Text("T = 0.1", color=BLUE).scale(0.5).to_corner(UR)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(moderate_curve, low_curve),
            Transform(temp_label, low_temp_label)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Zero temperature (step function)
        zero_curve = create_fd_curve(0, RED)
        zero_temp_label = Text("T → 0", color=RED).scale(0.5).to_corner(UR)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(moderate_curve, zero_curve),
```

```python
class RookAttacks(ForgeScene):
    # Board dimensions and cell coordinates
    board_size = 8

    def get_cell_pos(self, row, col):
        # Center the board on the left side of the screen
        x_offset = -3.0
        y_offset = 0.0
        x = x_offset + (col - (self.board_size - 1) / 2) * self.cell_width
        y = y_offset + (row - (self.board_size - 1) / 2) * self.cell_width

    @beat("Create the chessboard grid", seconds=4)
    def create_board(self):
        # Generate the 8x8 grid of squares with alternating colors
        self.squares = VGroup()
        for r in range(self.board_size):
            for c in range(self.board_size):
                color = "#E0C097" if (r + c) % 2 == 1 else "#B8860B"
                sq = Square(side_length=self.cell_width, stroke_width=1, stroke_color=GRAY_D)
                sq.set_fill(color, opacity=0.8)
                sq.move_to(self.get_cell_pos(r, c))
                # Store coordinates on the square for later reference
                sq.row = r
                sq.col = c
                self.squares.add(sq)
                
        # Draw board border
        self.border = SurroundingRectangle(self.squares, color=WHITE, stroke_width=3, buff=0.05)
        
        # Title on the right side
        self.title = Text("Rook's Attack Range", font_size=40, color=BLUE_B).move_to([3.5, 2.5, 0])
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(sq, scale=0.9) for sq in self.squares], lag_ratio=0.01, run_time=1.8),
            Create(self.border, run_time=1.2)
        )
        self.play(Write(self.title), run_time=1.0)

    @beat("Place the Rook on the board", seconds=3)
    def place_rook(self):
        # We place the rook at a specific test cell (row 3, col 4)
        self.rook_row = 3
        self.rook_col = 4
        
        # Draw a simplified vector representation of a rook
        rook_design = VGroup(
            Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.15, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1),
            Rectangle(width=0.3, height=0.25, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1),
            Rectangle(width=0.45, height=0.1, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        ).arrange(UP, buff=0.02)
        
        rook_design.move_to(self.get_cell_pos(self.rook_row, self.rook_col))
        self.rook = rook_design
        
        # Highlight the starting square
        self.start_highlight = Square(
            side_length=self.cell_width, 
            stroke_width=3, 
            stroke_color=YELLOW
        ).move_to(self.get_cell_pos(self.rook_row, self.rook_col))
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.start_highlight),
            DrawBorderThenFill(self.rook),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Highlight the attacked horizontal and vertical squares", seconds=5)
    def highlight_attacks(self):
        # Compute attacked squares dynamically
        self.horizontal_targets = VGroup()
        self.vertical_targets = VGroup()
        
        for sq in self.squares:
            if sq.row == self.rook_row and sq.col != self.rook_col:
                self.horizontal_targets.add(sq)
            elif sq.col == self.rook_col and sq.row != self.rook_row:
                self.vertical_targets.add(sq)
                
        # Count values dynamically
        self.h_count = len(self.horizontal_targets)
        self.v_count = len(self.vertical_targets)
        
        # Create visual overlays for attacked squares
        self.h_overlays = VGroup(*[
            Square(side_length=self.cell_width - 0.05, fill_color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0)
            .move_to(sq.get_center()) for sq in self.horizontal_targets
        ])
        
        self.v_overlays = VGroup(*[

        ])

            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(o, scale=0.5) for o in self.v_overlays], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
```

```python
            FadeIn(self.point_a, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(self.label_a),
            FadeIn(self.point_b, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(self.label_b),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(1.0)

    @beat("Show a test point P with distance lines to A and B", seconds=4)
    def show_test_point(self):
        # Position P off-center
        self.point_p = Dot(color=YELLOW).shift(UP * 2 + LEFT * 1)
        self.label_p = MathTex("P", color=YELLOW).next_to(self.point_p, UP)

        # Lines PA and PB
        self.line_pa = always_redraw(lambda: Line(self.point_p.get_center(), self.point_a.get_center(), color=BLUE_E))
        self.line_pb = always_redraw(lambda: Line(self.point_p.get_center(), self.point_b.get_center(), color=BLUE_E))

        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.point_p, scale=0.5),
            FadeIn(self.label_p),
            Create(self.line_pa),
            Create(self.line_pb),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Move P around to show unequal distances
        self.play(self.point_p.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Define the condition: distance PA equals distance PB", seconds=4)
    def define_condition(self):
        # Move P to a position where PA = PB (on the y-axis)
        target_pos = np.array([0.0, 1.5, 0.0])
        
        equation = MathTex("PA = PB", color=YELLOW)
        equation.to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP * 1)

        self.play(
            self.point_p.animate.move_to(target_pos),
            self.label_p.animate.next_to(target_pos, UP),
            Write(equation),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Trace the locus as a perpendicular bisector", seconds=5)
    def trace_locus(self):
        # The locus is the y-axis (x = 0)
        locus_line = Line(DOWN * 3.5, UP * 3.5, color=GREEN)
        
        # Midpoint M
        midpoint = Dot(ORIGIN, color=GREEN)
        label_m = MathTex("M", color=GREEN).next_to(midpoint, DOWN + LEFT)

        right_angle = RightAngle(

            Line(ORIGIN, UP * 1.5),
            length=0.3,
            color=GREEN
        )

        explanation = Tex("Perpendicular Bisector", font_size=30, color=GREEN)
        explanation.next_to(locus_line, RIGHT).shift(UP * 2)

        # Fade out the single point P and its lines to show the full set of points
        self.play(
            FadeOut(self.point_p),
            FadeOut(self.label_p),
            FadeOut(self.line_pa),
            FadeOut(self.line_pb),
            Create(locus_line),
            FadeIn(midpoint),
            FadeIn(label_m),
            Create(right_angle),
            Write(explanation),
            run_time=3.0
        )
        self.wait(2.0)
```

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class FareySequenceScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title slide
        title = Text("Unveiling Chord Patterns: Farey Sequences on the Unit Circle")
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        
        # Introduction to Farey sequences
        intro_text = Text("The Farey sequence orders rational numbers between 0 and 1")
        self.play(Write(intro_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro_text))
        
        # Definition of Farey sequence
        farey_def = MathTex(r"F_n = \{ \frac{a}{b} : 0 \leq a \leq b \leq n, \text{gcd}(a, b) = 1 \}")
        self.play(Write(farey_def))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(farey_def))
        
        # Create a unit circle
        circle = Circle(radius=3, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Farey sequence of order 4
        fractions = [(0, 1), (1, 4), (1, 3), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (1, 1)]
        
        # Function to convert fraction to point on unit circle
        def fraction_to_point(a, b):
            angle = 2 * np.pi * a / b
            return np.array([3 * np.cos(angle), 3 * np.sin(angle), 0])
        
        # Add points for each fraction
        dots = []
        labels = []
        
        for a, b in fractions:
            point = fraction_to_point(a, b)
            dot = Dot(point, color=YELLOW)
            label = MathTex(f"{a}/{b}")
            label.next_to(dot, direction=point/np.linalg.norm(point), buff=0.3)
            
            self.play(Create(dot), Write(label), run_time=0.5)
            dots.append(dot)
            labels.append(label)
        
        # Show the angle formula
        angle_formula = MathTex(r"\theta = 2\pi \frac{a}{b}")
        angle_formula.to_corner(UL)
        self.play(Write(angle_formula))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Draw chords between sequential fractions
        chords = []
        for i in range(len(fractions) - 1):
            p1 = fraction_to_point(fractions[i][0], fractions[i][1])
            p2 = fraction_to_point(fractions[i+1][0], fractions[i+1][1])
            chord = Line(p1, p2, color=RED)
            self.play(Create(chord), run_time=0.5)
            chords.append(chord)
        
        # Highlight the pattern
        insight_text = Text("Notice the pattern of chords")
        insight_text.to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(insight_text))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(insight_text))
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion = Text("Farey Sequence – A Journey Through Arithmetic & Geometry")
        conclusion.to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade everything out
        self.play(*[FadeOut(obj) for obj in [*dots, *labels, *chords, angle_formula, conclusion, circle]])
```

```python
from manim import *

class Count(Animation):
    def __init__(self, number: DecimalNumber, start: float, end: float, **kwargs) -> None:
        # Pass number as the mobject of the animation
        super().__init__(number,  **kwargs)
        # Set start and end
        self.start = start
        self.end = end

    def interpolate_mobject(self, alpha: float) -> None:
        # Set value of DecimalNumber according to alpha
        value = self.start + (alpha * (self.end - self.start))
        self.mobject.set_value(value)


class CountingScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Create Decimal Number and add it to scene
        number = DecimalNumber().set_color(WHITE).scale(5)
        # Add an updater to keep the DecimalNumber centered as its value changes
        number.add_updater(lambda number: number.move_to(ORIGIN))

        self.add(number)

        self.wait()

        # Play the Count Animation to count from 0 to 100 in 4 seconds
        self.play(Count(number, 0, 100), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)

        self.wait()
```

```python
        # Define the values for a 5-row Pascal's Triangle
        values = [
            [1],
            [1, 1],
            [1, 2, 1],
            [1, 3, 3, 1],
            [1, 4, 6, 4, 1]
        ]

        triangle = VGroup()
        
        for i, row in enumerate(values):

                group = VGroup(cell, number)
                group.move_to([j - (len(row)-1)/2, -i, 0])
                
                row_group.add(group)
            triangle.add(row_group)
        
        triangle.scale(0.8)
        return triangle
    
    def explain_formation(self, triangle):
        # Simple explanation of how entries are formed
        subtitle = Text("Each entry is the sum of the two above it", font_size=28, color=WHITE)

        # Clean up

            cell2[0].animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.2),

        # Create formulas for each row

            MathTex(r"1 + 1 = 2^1 = 2", color=WHITE),
            MathTex(r"1 + 2 + 1 = 2^2 = 4", color=WHITE),
            MathTex(r"1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 2^3 = 8", color=WHITE),

        # Position all formulas

        # Fade out the last formula and subtitle

    def show_binomial_connection(self):
```

```python
from manim import *
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat

class CollatzBouncer(ForgeScene):
    @beat("Introduce the Collatz rule: even halves, odd triples-plus-one", seconds=3)
    def introduce_rule(self):
        title = Text("The Collatz Conjecture", font_size=40, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        rule_even = MathTex(r"n \rightarrow \frac{n}{2}", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
        rule_odd = MathTex(r"n \rightarrow 3n + 1", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        
        rules = VGroup(
            Text("If even:", font_size=30), rule_even,
            Text("If odd:", font_size=30), rule_odd
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).shift(LEFT * 3)

        self.play(Write(title), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(rules, shift=RIGHT), run_time=2)

    @beat("Trace the sequence from 6 down to 1", seconds=3)
    def trace_sequence(self):
        # Compute Collatz sequence for 6 step-by-step
        n = 6
        seq = [n]
        while n > 1:
            if n % 2 == 0:
                n = n // 2
            else:
                n = 3 * n + 1
            seq.append(n)

        # seq will be [6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1]
        seq_tex = MathTex(
            r" \rightarrow ".join(str(x) for x in seq),
            font_size=36
        ).shift(RIGHT * 1.5)

        note = Text(f"Length: {len(seq)} steps", font_size=28, color=GRAY).next_to(seq_tex, DOWN, buff=0.8)

        self.play(Write(seq_tex), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP), run_time=1)
```

```python
        # Title
```

```python
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(title))

        intro_text = Text("Exploring patterns in combinatorial set theory", font_size=24)
        self.play(Write(intro_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(intro_text))
        
        # Key concept 1: Dots and lines
        # Create a set of points in a grid
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point) for point in [
            [-2, -1, 0], [0, -1, 0], [2, -1, 0],
            [-2, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0], [2, 1, 0]
        ]])
        
        # Animate the appearance of dots
        self.play(Create(dots))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Connect dots with lines
        lines = VGroup()
        for i, dot1 in enumerate(dots):
            for j, dot2 in enumerate(dots):
                if i < j:  # To avoid duplicate lines
                    line = Line(dot1.get_center(), dot2.get_center())
                    lines.add(line)
        
        # Animate the appearance of lines
        self.play(Create(lines))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Color some lines red (every third line)
        red_lines = []
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            if i % 3 == 0:
                red_lines.append(line.animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Only play animation if we have lines to color
        if red_lines:

        concept1_text = Text("Simple connections between points", font_size=20).to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(concept1_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Key concept 2: Hypergraph
        self.play(FadeOut(lines), FadeOut(concept1_text))
        
        # Rearrange dots into a circle
        circle_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(2*np.array([np.cos(i*2*PI/6), np.sin(i*2*PI/6), 0])) for i in range(6)])
        
        self.play(Transform(dots, circle_dots))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Create triangles (hyperedges) - just a few for simplicity
        triangles = VGroup()
        triangle_indices = [(0, 2, 4), (1, 3, 5), (0, 1, 2)]

            triangle = Polygon(
                dots[i].get_center(),
```

```python
        discrete_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # Create a simple grid of points (like stars in the sky)
        points = VGroup()
        for x in [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]:
            for y in [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]:
                point = Dot([x, y, 0], radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
                points.add(point)
        
        self.play(Write(discrete_text))
        self.play(Create(points))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 2. Points begin to connect
        connect_text = Text("Points begin to connect", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        connect_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # Create simple connections between adjacent points
        connections = VGroup()
        for i, p1 in enumerate(points):
            for j, p2 in enumerate(points[i+1:], i+1):
                # Only connect adjacent points
                dist = np.linalg.norm(p1.get_center() - p2.get_center())
                if dist <= 1.5:
                    line = Line(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), stroke_width=1, color=BLUE_C)
                    connections.add(line)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(discrete_text, connect_text))
        self.play(Create(connections))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 3. Convergent sequence
        sequence_text = Text("Sequences converge to limit points", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        sequence_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # Simple sequence converging to origin
        sequence = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 6):
            dot = Dot([3/i, 0, 0], radius=0.1, color=YELLOW)
            sequence.add(dot)
        
        limit_point = Dot([0, 0, 0], radius=0.15, color=RED)
        
        # Limit equation
        limit_eq = MathTex(r"\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n", color=WHITE)
        limit_eq.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(connect_text, sequence_text))
        self.play(Create(sequence))
        self.play(Create(limit_point))
        self.play(Write(limit_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 4. Compact space
        compact_text = Text("Compact Space", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        compact_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # More connections for compact space
        compact_connections = VGroup()
        for i, p1 in enumerate(points):
            for j, p2 in enumerate(points[i+1:], i+1):
                # Connect more points in compact space
                dist = np.linalg.norm(p1.get_center() - p2.get_center())
                if dist <= 3.0:  # Larger radius to include more connections
                    line = Line(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), stroke_width=1.5, color=BLUE_C)
                    compact_connections.add(line)
        
        # Heine-Borel theorem
        heine_borel = MathTex(r"\text{Closed and bounded} \rightarrow \text{compact}", color=WHITE)
        heine_borel.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(sequence_text, compact_text))
        self.play(FadeOut(sequence), FadeOut(limit_point))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(limit_eq, heine_borel))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(connections, compact_connections))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        conclusion = Text("From isolated points to a connected network", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        conclusion.to_edge(DOWN, buff=2)

        )
```

```python
from manim import *
from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
import numpy as np

class CompareAndSwapSort(ForgeScene):
    values = [1.5, 3.8, 2.0, 4.2, 2.9]
    idx1, idx2 = 1, 2  # Indices of adjacent elements to compare

    def get_x(self, index):
        return -3.0 + index * 1.5

    def make_bar(self, val, index, color=BLUE_C):
        rect = Rectangle(
            width=1.0,
            height=val,
            fill_opacity=0.85,
            fill_color=color,
            stroke_color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        pos = np.array([self.get_x(index), -1.8 + val / 2.0, 0])
        rect.move_to(pos)
        lbl = DecimalNumber(
            val,
            num_decimal_places=1,
            font_size=24,
            color=WHITE
        ).next_to(rect, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        return VGroup(rect, lbl)

    @beat("Compare adjacent elements in array", seconds=3)
    def compare_elements(self):
        self.bars = VGroup(*[
            self.make_bar(val, i) for i, val in enumerate(self.values)
        ])

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b, shift=UP * 0.3) for b in self.bars], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=1.2
        )

        v1, v2 = self.values[self.idx1], self.values[self.idx2]
        needs_swap = v1 > v2  # dynamically evaluated condition

        highlight1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx1, color=RED_C)
        highlight2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx2, color=RED_C)

        comp_op = ">" if needs_swap else "≤"
        action = "Swap Needed" if needs_swap else "In Order"
        self.cmp_text = Text(
            f"{v1} {comp_op} {v2}  ({action})",
            font_size=28,
            color=RED_C
        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)

        self.play(
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx1], highlight1),
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx2], highlight2),
            Write(self.cmp_text),
            run_time=1.3
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Swap out-of-order bars", seconds=3)
    def swap_elements(self):
        v1, v2 = self.values[self.idx1], self.values[self.idx2]

        # Target center locations after swap
        target_pos1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx2).get_center()
        target_pos2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx1).get_center()

        path1 = ArcBetweenPoints(self.bars[self.idx1].get_center(), target_pos1, angle=-PI / 2)
        path2 = ArcBetweenPoints(self.bars[self.idx2].get_center(), target_pos2, angle=-PI / 2)

        swapped1 = self.make_bar(v1, self.idx2, color=GREEN_C)
        swapped2 = self.make_bar(v2, self.idx1, color=GREEN_C)

        sorted_text = Text(
            f"{v2} < {v1}  (Sorted)",
            font_size=28,
            color=GREEN_C
        ).to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)

        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(self.bars[self.idx1], path1),
            MoveAlongPath(self.bars[self.idx2], path2),
            Transform(self.cmp_text, sorted_text),
            run_time=1.8
        )

        self.play(
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx1], swapped1),
            Transform(self.bars[self.idx2], swapped2),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(0.4)
```

```python
        # Create vectors

        self.w_arrow = Arrow(origin, self.plane.coords_to_point(*self.w_coord), buff=0, color=BLUE)
        
        # Labels
        self.v_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}", color=YELLOW).next_to(self.v_arrow.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        self.w_label = MathTex("\\vec{w}", color=BLUE).next_to(self.w_arrow.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)
        
        # Explanatory text on the right
        self.title = Text("Linear Independence", font_size=32).move_to([4, 1.5, 0])
        self.status = Text("Span 2D Space", color=GREEN, font_size=24).move_to([4, 0.8, 0])
        
        self.play(
            Create(self.plane),
            GrowArrow(self.v_arrow),
            GrowArrow(self.w_arrow),
            FadeIn(self.v_label),
            FadeIn(self.w_label),
            Write(self.title),
            FadeIn(self.status),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Collapse vectors onto one line to show dependence", seconds=3)
    def collapse_vectors(self):
        origin = self.plane.coords_to_point(0, 0)
        
        # Compute a dependent coordinate for w (scalar multiple of v)
        scalar = -1.5
        w_coord_new = scalar * self.v_coord
        
        # Define the target collapsed arrow
        new_w_arrow = Arrow(origin, self.plane.coords_to_point(*w_coord_new), buff=0, color=BLUE)
        
        # Compute the scalar factor dynamically to show on screen
        computed_scalar = w_coord_new[0] / self.v_coord[0]
        relation = MathTex(
            rf"\vec{{w}} = {computed_scalar:.1f} \vec{{v}}", 
            font_size=28
        ).move_to([4, -0.5, 0])
        
        new_status = Text("Linearly Dependent\n(Span 1D Line)", color=RED, font_size=24, line_spacing=0.8).move_to([4, 0.8, 0])
        
        # Draw the 1D span line
        span_line = Line(
            self.plane.coords_to_point(-4, -2),
            self.plane.coords_to_point(4, 2),
            color=YELLOW,
            stroke_width=2,
            stroke_opacity=0.5
        )

            Transform(self.w_arrow, new_w_arrow),
            self.w_label.animate.next_to(new_w_arrow.get_end(), DL, buff=0.1),

            Write(relation),
            run_time=2.5
        )
```

```python
BAD_C = "#FC6255"
SLOW_C = "#F0AC5F"

X_LO, X_HI = -5.0, 5.0


def loss(x: float) -> float:
    return 0.35 * x ** 2 + 0.4 * x + 1.2


class LearningRate(ForgeScene):

    x0 = 3.4

    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------------

    def make_axes(self) -> Axes:
        return Axes(
            x_range=[X_LO, X_HI, 1], y_range=[0, 11, 2],
            x_length=7.4, y_length=4.9,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2,
                         "color": GREY_B, "font_size": 20},
        ).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.35)

    def on_curve(self, x: float):
        return self.axes.c2p(x, loss(x))

    def run_descent(self, lr: float, n: int = 14) -> Descent:
        return Descent(loss, x0=self.x0, lr=lr, n_steps=n)

    def panel_text(self, *lines, color=WHITE, size=26) -> VGroup:
        return VGroup(*[Text(l, font_size=size, color=color) for l in lines]) \
            .arrange(DOWN, buff=0.16, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 1.4, 0])

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw the loss curve and mark its true minimum", seconds=5)
    def setup_curve(self):
        self.axes = self.make_axes()
        self.curve = self.axes.plot(loss, x_range=[X_LO, X_HI], color=CURVE_C,
                                    stroke_width=4)
        self.title = Text("Gradient descent", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)

        min_x, min_y = minimum_of(loss, X_LO, X_HI)     # found, not assumed
        self.min_dot = Dot(self.axes.c2p(min_x, min_y), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.07)
        # Below the x-axis, not between dot and axis: the curve's minimum sits
        # close enough to y=0 that a label placed under the dot lands on the
        # tick marks.
        self.min_label = Text("minimum", font_size=20, color=GOOD_C)
        self.min_label.next_to(self.axes.c2p(min_x, 0), DOWN, buff=0.28)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), Create(self.axes), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=1.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.min_dot, scale=0.5), Write(self.min_label), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Place a ball on the slope and show the gradient", seconds=5)
    def show_gradient(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        g = d.steps[0].grad

        self.ball = Dot(self.on_curve(self.x0), color=BALL_C, radius=0.11)
        span = 1.15
        tangent = Line(
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 - span, loss(self.x0) - g * span),
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 + span, loss(self.x0) + g * span),
            color=BALL_C, stroke_width=3,
        )

        self.rule = self.panel_text("the slope tells you", "which way is downhill",
                                    color=GREY_B, size=23)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.ball, scale=0.4), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Create(tangent), FadeIn(self.rule, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(0.6)
        self.play(FadeOut(tangent), FadeOut(self.rule), run_time=0.5)

    @beat("A good learning rate walks the ball to the minimum", seconds=8)
    def good_rate(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.55", color=GOOD_C, size=30)
        self.play(FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.6)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps[:10]:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.045).set_opacity(0.55)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(
                self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.28, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine,
            )

        verdict = Text(f"settles at x = {d.final_x:.2f}", font_size=24, color=GOOD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too large a step and it climbs out of the valley", seconds=8)
    def too_large(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=3.5)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "3.5", color=BAD_C, size=30)

        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        # Only the steps still inside the frame can be drawn; the rest is the point.
        visible = [s for s in d.steps if X_LO < s.next_x < X_HI][:6]
        for s in visible:
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      run_time=0.32, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine)

        arrow = Arrow(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 1.4, 8.2), self.axes.c2p(X_HI, 10.4),
                      color=BAD_C, buff=0, stroke_width=5)
        gone = Text("off the chart", font_size=22, color=BAD_C).next_to(arrow, LEFT, buff=0.12)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 0.2, 10.0)).set_opacity(0.3),
                  GrowArrow(arrow), FadeIn(gone), run_time=0.9)

        verdict = Text(f"reaches x = {d.final_x:,.0f}", font_size=24, color=BAD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(gone), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict),
                  self.ball.animate.set_opacity(1.0), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too small and it never arrives", seconds=7)
    def too_small(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.15)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.15", color=SLOW_C, size=30)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=SLOW_C, radius=0.04).set_opacity(0.5)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.2)

        verdict = Text(f"only x = {d.final_x:.2f} after {len(d.steps)} steps",
                       font_size=22, color=SLOW_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("The three rates side by side", seconds=6)
    def compare(self):
        rows = VGroup()
        for lr, colour, note in ((0.15, SLOW_C, "too small"),
                                 (0.55, GOOD_C, "about right"),
                                 (3.5, BAD_C, "too large")):
            d = self.run_descent(lr)
            rows.add(VGroup(
                Text(f"{lr}", font_size=26, color=colour),
                Text(note, font_size=20, color=GREY_B),
            ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN))
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.34, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=RIGHT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.25, run_time=1.6))
        self.play(Indicate(rows[1], color=GOOD_C, scale_factor=1.12), run_time=0.9)
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
        integral_problem = MathTex(r"\iint_{S} (x^2 + y^2) dS")
        self.play(Write(integral_problem))

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(ReplacementTransform(final_solution, final_result))
```

```python
        v_lines = 7  # vertical lines

            y = rect_bottom[1] + (i * height / h_lines)
            line = Line(
                start=[rect_left[0], y, 0],
                end=[rect_left[0] + width, y, 0],
                stroke_width=1
            )
            grid.add(line)
        
        # Create vertical lines
        for i in range(1, v_lines):
            x = rect_left[0] + (i * width / v_lines)
            line = Line(
                start=[x, rect_bottom[1], 0],
                end=[x, rect_bottom[1] + height, 0],
                stroke_width=1
            )
            grid.add(line)
```

```python
            x_range=[-5, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
            axis_config={"color": BLUE}
        ).scale(0.9)  # Scale down slightly to fit better
        
        # Define normal distributions with different means
        mean1, mean2 = -1.5, 1.5
        std_dev = 1
        
        # Function to create normal distribution curve
        def normal_dist(x, mean=0, std_dev=1):
            return np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mean) / std_dev) ** 2) / (std_dev * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))
```

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class PellsEquation(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and introduction
        title = Text("Pell's Equation: Dancing on the Hyperbola", font_size=36)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.scale(0.7).to_edge(UP))
        
        # Initial equation
        eq1 = MathTex("x^2 - ny^2 = 1", font_size=36)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition to specific equation
        eq2 = MathTex("x^2 - 2y^2 = 1", font_size=36)
        self.play(Transform(eq1, eq2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(title), eq1.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Create a grid
        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=(-5, 5, 1),
            y_range=(-4, 4, 1),
            axis_config={"color": BLUE_D},
        )
        self.play(Create(grid))
        
        # Draw the hyperbola using a simple parametric function
        # For x^2 - 2y^2 = 1, we use the parametric form:
        # x = sqrt(2)*cosh(t), y = sinh(t)
        
        def hyperbola_func(t):
            return np.array([np.sqrt(2) * np.cosh(t), np.sinh(t), 0])
        
        def neg_hyperbola_func(t):
            return np.array([-np.sqrt(2) * np.cosh(t), np.sinh(t), 0])
        
        right_branch = ParametricFunction(
            hyperbola_func,
            t_range=[-2, 2, 0.01],
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        left_branch = ParametricFunction(
            neg_hyperbola_func,
            t_range=[-2, 2, 0.01],
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        hyperbola = VGroup(right_branch, left_branch)
        self.play(Create(hyperbola))
        
        # Show integer solutions
        solutions = [(1, 0), (3, 2), (-1, 0), (-3, 2), (3, -2), (-3, -2)]
        
        dots = []
        for x, y in solutions:

                label = Text(f"({x},{y})", font_size=16).next_to(dot, direction=UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
```

```python
            f"P(A) = \\frac{{{count_a}}}{{{total}}} = {frac}",

        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Introduce Event B and condition on it", seconds=4)
    def show_event_b_conditioning(self):
        # Event B: right two columns (indices where col % 4 >= 2) -> columns 2 and 3
        # Grid is 4x4: rows 0-3, cols 0-3. Indices:
        # Col 2,3 in row 0: 2, 3
        # Col 2,3 in row 1: 6, 7

    def compute_conditional(self):

        cond_frac = Fraction(intersection_count, b_count)

            font_size=42,
            color=YELLOW_C

        self.play(Write(cond_formula), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(2.0)
```

```python
"""Gold scene 002 — learning rate and gradient descent.

The whole scene is driven by ``forge.primitives.optimise.Descent``. Nothing
about any trajectory is authored: the ball goes where the update rule sends it,
the divergence diverges because the arithmetic diverges, and the reported final
positions are read off the run rather than typed in.

That is the property worth training on. A model that learns to draw a plausible
descent curve has learned decoration. A model that learns to *run the optimiser
and animate the result* has learned something true.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.optimise import Descent, minimum_of

CURVE_C = BLUE_C
BALL_C = YELLOW_C
GOOD_C = "#5CD0B3"
BAD_C = "#FC6255"
SLOW_C = "#F0AC5F"

X_LO, X_HI = -5.0, 5.0


def loss(x: float) -> float:
    return 0.35 * x ** 2 + 0.4 * x + 1.2


class LearningRate(ForgeScene):

    x0 = 3.4

    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------------

    def make_axes(self) -> Axes:
        return Axes(
            x_range=[X_LO, X_HI, 1], y_range=[0, 11, 2],
            x_length=7.4, y_length=4.9,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2,
                         "color": GREY_B, "font_size": 20},
        ).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.35)

    def on_curve(self, x: float):
        return self.axes.c2p(x, loss(x))

    def run_descent(self, lr: float, n: int = 14) -> Descent:
        return Descent(loss, x0=self.x0, lr=lr, n_steps=n)

    def panel_text(self, *lines, color=WHITE, size=26) -> VGroup:
        return VGroup(*[Text(l, font_size=size, color=color) for l in lines]) \
            .arrange(DOWN, buff=0.16, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 1.4, 0])

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw the loss curve and mark its true minimum", seconds=5)
    def setup_curve(self):
        self.axes = self.make_axes()
        self.curve = self.axes.plot(loss, x_range=[X_LO, X_HI], color=CURVE_C,
                                    stroke_width=4)
        self.title = Text("Gradient descent", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)

        min_x, min_y = minimum_of(loss, X_LO, X_HI)     # found, not assumed
        self.min_dot = Dot(self.axes.c2p(min_x, min_y), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.07)
        # Below the x-axis, not between dot and axis: the curve's minimum sits
        # close enough to y=0 that a label placed under the dot lands on the
        # tick marks.
        self.min_label = Text("minimum", font_size=20, color=GOOD_C)
        self.min_label.next_to(self.axes.c2p(min_x, 0), DOWN, buff=0.28)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), Create(self.axes), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Create(self.curve), run_time=1.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.min_dot, scale=0.5), Write(self.min_label), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Place a ball on the slope and show the gradient", seconds=5)
    def show_gradient(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        g = d.steps[0].grad

        self.ball = Dot(self.on_curve(self.x0), color=BALL_C, radius=0.11)
        span = 1.15
        tangent = Line(
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 - span, loss(self.x0) - g * span),
            self.axes.c2p(self.x0 + span, loss(self.x0) + g * span),
            color=BALL_C, stroke_width=3,
        )

        self.rule = self.panel_text("the slope tells you", "which way is downhill",
                                    color=GREY_B, size=23)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.ball, scale=0.4), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Create(tangent), FadeIn(self.rule, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=1.2)
        self.wait(0.6)
        self.play(FadeOut(tangent), FadeOut(self.rule), run_time=0.5)

    @beat("A good learning rate walks the ball to the minimum", seconds=8)
    def good_rate(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.55)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.55", color=GOOD_C, size=30)
        self.play(FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.6)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps[:10]:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=GOOD_C, radius=0.045).set_opacity(0.55)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(
                self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.28, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine,
            )

        verdict = Text(f"settles at x = {d.final_x:.2f}", font_size=24, color=GOOD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too large a step and it climbs out of the valley", seconds=8)
    def too_large(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=3.5)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "3.5", color=BAD_C, size=30)

        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        # Only the steps still inside the frame can be drawn; the rest is the point.
        visible = [s for s in d.steps if X_LO < s.next_x < X_HI][:6]
        for s in visible:
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      run_time=0.32, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine)

        arrow = Arrow(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 1.4, 8.2), self.axes.c2p(X_HI, 10.4),
                      color=BAD_C, buff=0, stroke_width=5)
        gone = Text("off the chart", font_size=22, color=BAD_C).next_to(arrow, LEFT, buff=0.12)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.axes.c2p(X_HI - 0.2, 10.0)).set_opacity(0.3),
                  GrowArrow(arrow), FadeIn(gone), run_time=0.9)

        verdict = Text(f"reaches x = {d.final_x:,.0f}", font_size=24, color=BAD_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.7)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(gone), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict),
                  self.ball.animate.set_opacity(1.0), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Too small and it never arrives", seconds=7)
    def too_small(self):
        d = self.run_descent(lr=0.15)
        label = self.panel_text("learning rate", "0.15", color=SLOW_C, size=30)
        self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(self.x0)),
                  FadeIn(label, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.7)

        trail = VGroup()
        for s in d.steps:
            mark = Dot(self.on_curve(s.x), color=SLOW_C, radius=0.04).set_opacity(0.5)
            trail.add(mark)
            self.play(self.ball.animate.move_to(self.on_curve(s.next_x)),
                      FadeIn(mark), run_time=0.2)

        verdict = Text(f"only x = {d.final_x:.2f} after {len(d.steps)} steps",
                       font_size=22, color=SLOW_C)
        verdict.next_to(label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(verdict), run_time=0.7)
        self.wait(0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(trail), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(verdict), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("The three rates side by side", seconds=6)
    def compare(self):
        rows = VGroup()
        for lr, colour, note in ((0.15, SLOW_C, "too small"),
                                 (0.55, GOOD_C, "about right"),
                                 (3.5, BAD_C, "too large")):
            d = self.run_descent(lr)
            rows.add(VGroup(
                Text(f"{lr}", font_size=26, color=colour),
                Text(note, font_size=20, color=GREY_B),
            ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=DOWN))
        rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.34, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to([4.2, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=RIGHT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.25, run_time=1.6))
        self.play(Indicate(rows[1], color=GOOD_C, scale_factor=1.12), run_time=0.9)
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
"""Gold scene 001 — rook mobility and corner probability.

Authored by hand from Nimit's own prompt:

    "build me a chess grid, add rooks on it and animate the rook's possible
     movements, then help me calculate the probability that if i place the
     rook at any square, it is a corner square"

This is a *target*, not a sample: the standard the fine-tuned model has to
reach. Two properties make it gold rather than merely working.

**Every number on screen is computed.** The 4, the 64 and the 1/16 come from
counting cells in ``forge.primitives.grid``. Nothing here recites a figure a
language model happened to remember.

**It answers more than it was asked.** The prompt requested rook movement and
corner probability as two separate things. Beat 4 finds the link worth showing:
a rook reaches exactly 14 squares from *every* square on the board, corners
included. That invariance came out of writing the primitive, and it is the
difference between a diagram and an explanation.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.grid import Board, Cell

# A restrained palette: neutral board, one colour for attention, one for the
# result. Loud boards fight the thing you are trying to point at.
LIGHT_SQ = "#3D4852"
DARK_SQ = "#2A313A"
ROOK_C = BLUE_C
REACH_C = YELLOW_C
CORNER_C = "#5CD0B3"

CELL = 0.70
BOARD_X = -3.1      # board centre; right half is the information panel
PANEL_X = 3.4


def rook_glyph(color=ROOK_C) -> VGroup:
    """A rook built from primitives rather than a font glyph — no typeface to
    be missing, and it scales cleanly."""
    base = Rectangle(width=0.40, height=0.07, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem = Rectangle(width=0.24, height=0.24, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    head = Rectangle(width=0.36, height=0.10, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem.next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
    head.next_to(stem, UP, buff=0)
    return VGroup(base, stem, head)


class RookCorners(ForgeScene):

    board = Board(8, 8)

    # -- geometry helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def xy(self, cell: Cell) -> np.ndarray:
        """Cell -> world coordinates, with the board centred on the origin."""
        x = BOARD_X + (cell.col - (self.board.cols - 1) / 2) * CELL
        y = (cell.row - (self.board.rows - 1) / 2) * CELL - 0.3
        return np.array([x, y, 0.0])

    def tile(self, cell: Cell, color, opacity=0.85) -> Square:
        return Square(side_length=CELL, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=color, fill_opacity=opacity).move_to(self.xy(cell))

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw an 8x8 chessboard", seconds=3)
    def draw_board(self):
        self.squares = VGroup(*[
            self.tile(c, LIGHT_SQ if self.board.is_light(c) else DARK_SQ, 1.0)
            for c in self.board.cells()
        ])
        self.title = Text("A rook on an 8 x 8 board", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s, scale=0.6) for s in self.squares],
                              lag_ratio=0.012, run_time=2.0))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)

    @beat("Place a rook on d4", seconds=2)
    def place_rook(self):
        self.origin = Cell(3, 3)                      # d4
        self.rook = rook_glyph().move_to(self.xy(self.origin))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.rook, shift=UP * 0.4), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(self.rook, color=ROOK_C, line_length=0.16, num_lines=10,
                        flash_radius=0.42), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight every square the rook can reach", seconds=5)
    def show_reach(self):
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(self.origin)     # computed, not hardcoded
        self.reach_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.count = VGroup(
            Text(str(len(reach)), font_size=72, color=REACH_C),
            Text("reachable squares", font_size=24, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.18).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t) for t in self.reach_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.05, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.count[0], scale=0.7), Write(self.count[1]), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.4)

    @beat("Move the rook to the corner - the count is unchanged", seconds=5)
    def corner_is_no_different(self):
        corner = Cell(0, 0)                            # a1
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(corner)
        new_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.play(
            self.rook.animate.move_to(self.xy(corner)),
            Transform(self.reach_tiles, new_tiles),
            run_time=1.6,
        )
        # The count is unchanged, so the numeral must visibly hold still while
        # everything around it moves — that stillness *is* the point of the beat.
        self.play(Indicate(self.count[0], color=REACH_C, scale_factor=1.25), run_time=0.8)

        note = VGroup(
            Text("still 14.", font_size=28, color=REACH_C),
            Text("a rook's reach is the", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
            Text("same from every square", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.12).move_to([PANEL_X, -1.5, 0])
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.9)
        self.play(FadeOut(note), FadeOut(self.reach_tiles), FadeOut(self.count),
                  run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight the four corner squares", seconds=4)
    def show_corners(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()                 # computed -> 4
        self.corner_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, CORNER_C, 0.55) for c in corners])

        new_title = Text("How likely is a corner?", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(Transform(self.title, new_title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rook, shift=DOWN * 0.3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(t) for t in self.corner_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.4))
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Derive the probability as an exact fraction", seconds=6)
    def derive(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()
        p = self.board.probability_of(corners)         # Fraction(1, 16) - exact

        expr = MathTex(
            r"P(\text{corner})", "=",
            rf"\frac{{{len(corners)}}}{{{self.board.n_cells}}}",
            font_size=42,
        ).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])
        expr[2].set_color(CORNER_C)

        reduced = MathTex("=", rf"\frac{{{p.numerator}}}{{{p.denominator}}}", font_size=52)
        reduced[1].set_color(CORNER_C)
        reduced.next_to(expr, DOWN, buff=0.45)

        self.play(Write(expr[0]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Write(expr[1]), Write(expr[2]), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(reduced), run_time=0.9)

        pct = Text(f"{float(p) * 100:.2f}%", font_size=26, color=GREY_B)
        pct.next_to(reduced, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(pct, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.6)
        self.expr, self.reduced, self.pct = expr, reduced, pct
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
            pos = self.clock_circle.get_center() + np.array([2.5 * np.cos(angle), 2.5 * np.sin(angle), 0])
            
            dot = Dot(pos, color=WHITE)
            self.hour_dots.add(dot)
            
            label_pos = self.clock_circle.get_center() + np.array([3.1 * np.cos(angle), 3.1 * np.sin(angle), 0])
            # Compute label using modular arithmetic
            val = i if i != 0 else self.modulus
            lbl = Text(str(val), font_size=24, color=YELLOW_C).move_to(label_pos)
            self.hour_labels.add(lbl)

        self.play(

            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in self.hour_dots], lag_ratio=0.05),

            run_time=2.5
        )

        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow1), run_time=1.0)
```

```python
        # Introduction - simple equation
        eq1 = Text("Sum: 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + ...")
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Comparison with integral
        eq2 = Text("Compared with: Integral of 1/x from 1 to infinity")
        eq2.next_to(eq1, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(eq2))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(eq1), FadeOut(eq2))
        
        # Set up coordinate system
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
        )
        x_label = Text("n", font_size=24)
        y_label = Text("Sum", font_size=24)
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        
        # Create harmonic series values
        harmonic_values = [0]  # Start at 0
        for n in range(1, 11):
            harmonic_values.append(harmonic_values[-1] + 1/n)
        
        # Create step function using lines
        step_lines = VGroup()
        
        for n in range(1, 11):
            # Horizontal line
            h_line = Line(
                axes.c2p(n-1, harmonic_values[n-1]),
                axes.c2p(n, harmonic_values[n-1]),
                color=BLUE
            )
            # Vertical line
            v_line = Line(
                axes.c2p(n, harmonic_values[n-1]),
                axes.c2p(n, harmonic_values[n]),
                color=BLUE
            )
            step_lines.add(h_line, v_line)
        
        # Draw natural log curve
        x_range = np.linspace(1, 10, 100)
        log_points = [axes.c2p(x, np.log(x)) for x in x_range]
```

```python
        ])

    @beat("Start at the root node A and initialize the queue", seconds=4, narration="We begin at the root node, A, and add it to our traversal queue.")
```

```python
        # Add slight noise
        self.y_vals = 0.2 * (self.x_vals - 2.5)**2 + 1.5 + np.array([0.2, -0.3, 0.4, -0.1, 0.3, -0.4, 0.1, 0.2])
        
        self.dots = VGroup(*[

        ])
```
