```python
        self.play(Create(self.axes), FadeIn(self.dots, lag_ratio=0.1, scale=0.5), run_time=2.0)
        self.play(Write(title), run_time=0.8)

    @beat("Show a simple, generalized model (underfitting/good fit)", seconds=4)
    def show_good_model(self):
        # A smooth quadratic curve
        curve_func = lambda x: 0.25 * (x - 2.5)**2 + 1.3
        self.good_curve = self.axes.plot(curve_func, x_range=[0.2, 5.5], color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)
        
        label = Text("True Pattern\n(Generalizes Well)", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        label.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=0.8).shift(UP * 1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(self.good_curve), Write(label), run_time=3.0)

    @beat("Transition to an overly complex, wiggly model", seconds=5)
    def show_overfitted_model(self):
        # High-degree polynomial approximation passing through every single point
        poly = np.polyfit(self.x_vals, self.y_vals, deg=7)
        wiggly_func = lambda x: np.polyval(poly, x)
        
        self.wiggly_curve = self.axes.plot(wiggly_func, x_range=[0.3, 5.4], color=RED, stroke_width=3)
        
        warning_label = Text("Overfitting:\nChasing every noise point", font_size=24, color=RED)
```

```python
        )
```

```python
        c4_label = Text("C4", font_size=36).next_to(c4, UP)

            position = c2_radius * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            dot = Dot(position, color=RED)
            label = Text(f"h{i}", font_size=24)
            # Calculate the direction outward from center
            direction = position / np.linalg.norm(position) if np.linalg.norm(position) > 0 else RIGHT
            label.next_to(dot, direction, buff=0.2)
            c2_dots.append(VGroup(dot, label))
        
        c2 = VGroup(*c2_dots).shift(RIGHT * 3)

        # Add Cayley graph edges
        edges_c4 = []
        for i in range(4):
            start = c4_dots[i][0].get_center()

            edge = Arrow(start, end, buff=0.2, color=GREEN)

            edge = Arrow(start, end, buff=0.2, color=GREEN)
            edges_c2.append(edge)

        self.play(*[Create(edge) for edge in edges_c2])
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show homomorphism equation

        self.play(Write(eq2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show homomorphism mappings
        mappings = []
        # g0 -> h0, g2 -> h0
        for i in [0, 2]:
            start = c4_dots[i][0].get_center()
            end = c2_dots[0][0].get_center()
            mapping = Arrow(start, end, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
```

```python
class BreadthFirstSearchExplainer(ForgeScene):
    
    @beat("Initialize graph structure and node positions", seconds=3)
    def setup_graph(self):
        # Define vertices and edges for BFS tree
        self.node_coords = {
            'A': np.array([-4.5, 2.0, 0]),
            'B': np.array([-2.0, 3.2, 0]),
            'C': np.array([-2.0, 0.8, 0]),
            'D': np.array([0.5, 3.8, 0]),
            'E': np.array([0.5, 2.0, 0]),
            'F': np.array([0.5, -0.2, 0]),
            'G': np.array([3.0, 1.0, 0]),
        }
        
        self.adj_list = {
            'A': ['B', 'C'],
            'B': ['A', 'D', 'E'],
            'C': ['A', 'F'],
            'D': ['B'],
            'E': ['B', 'G'],
            'F': ['C', 'G'],
            'E_list': [('A', 'B'), ('A', 'C'), ('B', 'D'), ('B', 'E'), ('C', 'F'), ('E', 'G'), ('F', 'G')]
        }

        self.edges = VGroup()
        for u, v in self.adj_list['E_list']:
            line = Line(self.node_coords[u], self.node_coords[v], color=GRAY, stroke_width=3)
            self.edges.add(line)

        self.vertices = VGroup()
        self.node_mobs = {}
        for name, coord in self.node_coords.items():
            circle = Circle(radius=0.45, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1)
            text = Text(name, font_size=32, color=WHITE)
            node = VGroup(circle, text).move_to(coord)
            self.node_mobs[name] = node
            self.vertices.add(node)

        self.play(FadeIn(self.edges), FadeIn(self.vertices), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(0.5)

    @beat("Introduce BFS and the Queue data structure", seconds=4)
    def introduce_bfs(self):
        title = Text("Breadth-First Search (BFS)", font_size=36, color=BLUE_C).to_edge(UP)
        title.shift(LEFT * 2)
        
        queue_box = Rectangle(width=4.5, height=1.0, color=YELLOW_C).to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP * 2.5)
        queue_label = Text("Queue (FIFO)", font_size=24, color=YELLOW_C).next_to(queue_box, UP)
        
        self.queue_content = VGroup()
        self.queue_container = VGroup(queue_box, queue_label)
        
        self.play(Write(title), FadeIn(self.queue_container), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1.0)

    @beat("Enqueue starting node A", seconds=4)
    def start_bfs(self):
        # Highlight node A
        self.play(
            self.node_mobs['A'][0].animate.set_color(BLUE),
            self.node_mobs['A'][1].animate.set_color(BLUE),
            run_time=1.0

        self.q_text.move_to(self.queue_container[0].get_center())
        self.play(Write(self.q_text), run_time=1.0)
        
        self.visited = set(['A'])
        self.queue = deque(['A'])
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Dequeue A and explore its neighbors B and C", seconds=5)
    def explore_a(self):
        curr = self.queue.popleft() # 'A'

        new_q_text = Text("[ B, C ]", font_size=32, color=YELLOW_C).move_to(self.queue_container[0].get_center())

        )

    def explore_c(self):

        new_q_text = Text("[ D, E, F ]", font_size=32, color=YELLOW_C).move_to(self.queue_container[0].get_center())
```

```python
class SineCurveUnitCircle(Scene):

    def construct(self):
        self.show_axis()
        self.show_circle()
        self.move_dot_and_draw_curve()
        self.wait()

        x_start = np.array([-6,0,0])
        x_end = np.array([6,0,0])

        y_start = np.array([-4,-2,0])
        y_end = np.array([-4,2,0])

        x_axis = Line(x_start, x_end)
        y_axis = Line(y_start, y_end)

        self.add(x_axis, y_axis)
        self.add_x_labels()

        self.origin_point = np.array([-4,0,0])
        self.curve_start = np.array([-3,0,0])

    def add_x_labels(self):
        x_labels = [
            MathTex(r"\pi"), MathTex(r"2 \pi"),
            MathTex(r"3 \pi"), MathTex(r"4 \pi"),
        ]

        for i in range(len(x_labels)):
            x_labels[i].next_to(np.array([-1 + 2*i, 0, 0]), DOWN)
            self.add(x_labels[i])

    def show_circle(self):
        circle = Circle(radius=1)
        circle.move_to(self.origin_point)
        self.add(circle)
        self.circle = circle

    def move_dot_and_draw_curve(self):
        orbit = self.circle
        origin_point = self.origin_point

        dot = Dot(radius=0.08, color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(orbit.point_from_proportion(0))
        self.t_offset = 0
        rate = 0.25

        def go_around_circle(mob, dt):
            self.t_offset += (dt * rate)
            # print(self.t_offset)
            mob.move_to(orbit.point_from_proportion(self.t_offset % 1))

        def get_line_to_circle():
            return Line(origin_point, dot.get_center(), color=BLUE)

        def get_line_to_curve():
            x = self.curve_start[0] + self.t_offset * 4
            y = dot.get_center()[1]
            return Line(dot.get_center(), np.array([x,y,0]), color=YELLOW_A, stroke_width=2 )


        self.curve = VGroup()
        self.curve.add(Line(self.curve_start,self.curve_start))
        def get_curve():
            last_line = self.curve[-1]
            x = self.curve_start[0] + self.t_offset * 4
            y = dot.get_center()[1]
            new_line = Line(last_line.get_end(),np.array([x,y,0]), color=YELLOW_D)
            self.curve.add(new_line)

            return self.curve

        dot.add_updater(go_around_circle)

        origin_to_circle_line = always_redraw(get_line_to_circle)
        dot_to_curve_line = always_redraw(get_line_to_curve)
        sine_curve_line = always_redraw(get_curve)

        self.add(dot)
        self.add(orbit, origin_to_circle_line, dot_to_curve_line, sine_curve_line)
        self.wait(8.5)

        dot.remove_updater(go_around_circle)
```

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class ExtremalValueTheory(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title
        title = Text("Unleashing the Extremes: Block Maxima vs. Peaks-Over-Threshold", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP).scale(0.8))
        
        # Create axes for time series
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
        ).scale(0.8).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Add labels
        x_label = Text("Time", font_size=20).next_to(axes, DOWN)
        y_label = Text("Value", font_size=20).next_to(axes, LEFT)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        
        # Create time series data (using sine wave for simplicity)
        x_values = np.linspace(0, 10, 50)
        y_values = np.sin(x_values)
        points = [axes.c2p(x, y) for x, y in zip(x_values, y_values)]
        time_series = Line().set_points_smoothly(points).set_color(BLUE)
        
        self.play(Create(time_series))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Block Maxima approach
        bm_title = Text("Block Maxima Approach", color=BLUE).next_to(title, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(bm_title))
        
        # Create blocks
        blocks = VGroup()
        max_dots = VGroup()
        
        for i in range(3):
            # Block boundaries
            x_start = i * 3.33
            x_end = (i + 1) * 3.33
            
            # Create visual block
            block = Rectangle(
                width=3.33 * axes.x_axis.unit_size,
                height=4 * axes.y_axis.unit_size,
                fill_color=BLUE,
                fill_opacity=0.2,
                stroke_width=1
            ).move_to(axes.c2p((x_start + x_end)/2, 0))
            blocks.add(block)
            
            # Find maximum in this block
            block_indices = (x_values >= x_start) & (x_values < x_end)
            if np.any(block_indices):
                block_y = y_values[block_indices]
                max_idx = np.argmax(block_y)
                max_x = x_values[block_indices][max_idx]
                max_y = block_y[max_idx]
                
                # Create dot for maximum
                max_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(max_x, max_y), color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
                max_dots.add(max_dot)
        
        self.play(Create(blocks))
        self.play(Create(max_dots))
        
        # Equation for Block Maxima
        bm_eq = MathTex("M_n = \\max(X_1, X_2, \\ldots, X_n)")
        self.play(Write(bm_eq.next_to(bm_title, DOWN)))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clear for next approach
        self.play(
            FadeOut(blocks),
            FadeOut(max_dots),
            FadeOut(bm_title),
            FadeOut(bm_eq)
        )
        
        # Peaks-Over-Threshold approach
        pot_title = Text("Peaks-Over-Threshold Approach", color=RED).next_to(title, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(pot_title))
        
        # Define threshold
        threshold_value = 0.6
        threshold_line = DashedLine(
            start=axes.c2p(0, threshold_value),
            end=axes.c2p(10, threshold_value),
            color=RED
        )
        threshold_label = Text("Threshold (u)", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(threshold_line, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(threshold_line), Write(threshold_label))
        
        # Find points exceeding threshold
        peak_dots = VGroup()
        for x, y in zip(x_values, y_values):
            if y > threshold_value:
                dot = Dot(axes.c2p(x, y), color=RED, radius=0.08)
                peak_dots.add(dot)
        
        self.play(Create(peak_dots))
        
        # Equation for Peaks-Over-Threshold
        pot_eq = MathTex("Y_i = X_i - u \\mid X_i > u")
        self.play(Write(pot_eq.next_to(pot_title, DOWN)))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Conclusion
        self.play(
            FadeOut(pot_title),
            FadeOut(pot_eq),
            FadeOut(threshold_line),
            FadeOut(threshold_label),
            FadeOut(peak_dots)
        )
        
        conclusion = Text("Different approaches, complementary insights", 
                         font_size=28).next_to(title, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final fade out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(conclusion),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(time_series),
            FadeOut(x_label),
            FadeOut(y_label),
            FadeOut(title)
        )
        
        thank_you = Text("Thank you for exploring extremes with us!", font_size=32)
        self.play(Write(thank_you))
        self.wait(2)
```

```python
"""Gold scene 001 — rook mobility and corner probability.

Authored by hand from Nimit's own prompt:

    "build me a chess grid, add rooks on it and animate the rook's possible
     movements, then help me calculate the probability that if i place the
     rook at any square, it is a corner square"

This is a *target*, not a sample: the standard the fine-tuned model has to
reach. Two properties make it gold rather than merely working.

**Every number on screen is computed.** The 4, the 64 and the 1/16 come from
counting cells in ``forge.primitives.grid``. Nothing here recites a figure a
language model happened to remember.

**It answers more than it was asked.** The prompt requested rook movement and
corner probability as two separate things. Beat 4 finds the link worth showing:
a rook reaches exactly 14 squares from *every* square on the board, corners
included. That invariance came out of writing the primitive, and it is the
difference between a diagram and an explanation.
"""

from manim import *

from forge.beats import ForgeScene, beat
from forge.primitives.grid import Board, Cell

# A restrained palette: neutral board, one colour for attention, one for the
# result. Loud boards fight the thing you are trying to point at.
LIGHT_SQ = "#3D4852"
DARK_SQ = "#2A313A"
ROOK_C = BLUE_C
REACH_C = YELLOW_C
CORNER_C = "#5CD0B3"

CELL = 0.70
BOARD_X = -3.1      # board centre; right half is the information panel
PANEL_X = 3.4


def rook_glyph(color=ROOK_C) -> VGroup:
    """A rook built from primitives rather than a font glyph — no typeface to
    be missing, and it scales cleanly."""
    base = Rectangle(width=0.40, height=0.07, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem = Rectangle(width=0.24, height=0.24, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    head = Rectangle(width=0.36, height=0.10, fill_opacity=1, color=color, stroke_width=0)
    stem.next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
    head.next_to(stem, UP, buff=0)
    return VGroup(base, stem, head)


class RookCorners(ForgeScene):

    board = Board(8, 8)

    # -- geometry helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def xy(self, cell: Cell) -> np.ndarray:
        """Cell -> world coordinates, with the board centred on the origin."""
        x = BOARD_X + (cell.col - (self.board.cols - 1) / 2) * CELL
        y = (cell.row - (self.board.rows - 1) / 2) * CELL - 0.3
        return np.array([x, y, 0.0])

    def tile(self, cell: Cell, color, opacity=0.85) -> Square:
        return Square(side_length=CELL, stroke_width=0,
                      fill_color=color, fill_opacity=opacity).move_to(self.xy(cell))

    # -- beats ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @beat("Draw an 8x8 chessboard", seconds=3)
    def draw_board(self):
        self.squares = VGroup(*[
            self.tile(c, LIGHT_SQ if self.board.is_light(c) else DARK_SQ, 1.0)
            for c in self.board.cells()
        ])
        self.title = Text("A rook on an 8 x 8 board", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s, scale=0.6) for s in self.squares],
                              lag_ratio=0.012, run_time=2.0))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title, shift=DOWN * 0.2), run_time=0.7)

    @beat("Place a rook on d4", seconds=2)
    def place_rook(self):
        self.origin = Cell(3, 3)                      # d4
        self.rook = rook_glyph().move_to(self.xy(self.origin))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.rook, shift=UP * 0.4), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(self.rook, color=ROOK_C, line_length=0.16, num_lines=10,
                        flash_radius=0.42), run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight every square the rook can reach", seconds=5)
    def show_reach(self):
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(self.origin)     # computed, not hardcoded
        self.reach_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.count = VGroup(
            Text(str(len(reach)), font_size=72, color=REACH_C),
            Text("reachable squares", font_size=24, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.18).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.6, 0])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t) for t in self.reach_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.05, run_time=1.8))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.count[0], scale=0.7), Write(self.count[1]), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.4)

    @beat("Move the rook to the corner - the count is unchanged", seconds=5)
    def corner_is_no_different(self):
        corner = Cell(0, 0)                            # a1
        reach = self.board.rook_moves(corner)
        new_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, REACH_C, 0.42) for c in reach])

        self.play(
            self.rook.animate.move_to(self.xy(corner)),
            Transform(self.reach_tiles, new_tiles),
            run_time=1.6,
        )
        # The count is unchanged, so the numeral must visibly hold still while
        # everything around it moves — that stillness *is* the point of the beat.
        self.play(Indicate(self.count[0], color=REACH_C, scale_factor=1.25), run_time=0.8)

        note = VGroup(
            Text("still 14.", font_size=28, color=REACH_C),
            Text("a rook's reach is the", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
            Text("same from every square", font_size=22, color=GREY_B),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.12).move_to([PANEL_X, -1.5, 0])
        self.play(FadeIn(note, shift=UP * 0.15), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.9)
        self.play(FadeOut(note), FadeOut(self.reach_tiles), FadeOut(self.count),
                  run_time=0.6)

    @beat("Highlight the four corner squares", seconds=4)
    def show_corners(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()                 # computed -> 4
        self.corner_tiles = VGroup(*[self.tile(c, CORNER_C, 0.55) for c in corners])

        new_title = Text("How likely is a corner?", font_size=30).to_edge(UP, buff=0.35)
        self.play(Transform(self.title, new_title), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.rook, shift=DOWN * 0.3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(t) for t in self.corner_tiles],
                              lag_ratio=0.15, run_time=1.4))
        self.wait(0.3)

    @beat("Derive the probability as an exact fraction", seconds=6)
    def derive(self):
        corners = self.board.corners()
        p = self.board.probability_of(corners)         # Fraction(1, 16) - exact

        expr = MathTex(
            r"P(\text{corner})", "=",
            rf"\frac{{{len(corners)}}}{{{self.board.n_cells}}}",
            font_size=42,
        ).move_to([PANEL_X, 0.9, 0])
        expr[2].set_color(CORNER_C)

        reduced = MathTex("=", rf"\frac{{{p.numerator}}}{{{p.denominator}}}", font_size=52)
        reduced[1].set_color(CORNER_C)
        reduced.next_to(expr, DOWN, buff=0.45)

        self.play(Write(expr[0]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(Write(expr[1]), Write(expr[2]), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(reduced), run_time=0.9)

        pct = Text(f"{float(p) * 100:.2f}%", font_size=26, color=GREY_B)
        pct.next_to(reduced, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(pct, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.6)
        self.expr, self.reduced, self.pct = expr, reduced, pct
        self.wait(1.0)
```

```python
class ThreeDSurfacePlot(ThreeDScene):
    def construct(self):
        resolution_fa = 24
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-30 * DEGREES)

        def param_gauss(u, v):
            x = u
            y = v
            sigma, mu = 0.4, [0.0, 0.0]
            d = np.linalg.norm(np.array([x - mu[0], y - mu[1]]))
            z = np.exp(-(d ** 2 / (2.0 * sigma ** 2)))
            return np.array([x, y, z])

        gauss_plane = Surface(
            param_gauss,
            resolution=(resolution_fa, resolution_fa),
            v_range=[-2, +2],
            u_range=[-2, +2]
        )

        gauss_plane.scale(2, about_point=ORIGIN)

        gauss_plane.set_fill_by_checkerboard(ORANGE, BLUE, opacity=0.5)
```

```python
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Write(phase_space), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Create particles (dancers)
        particles = VGroup()
        initial_positions = [
            axes.c2p(-2, 1),

            axes.c2p(-1, -1),

            particles.add(particle)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(particles))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Liouville Equation

        liouville_title = Text("The Liouville Equation:", color=BLUE_C, font_size=24).next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        liouville_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dt}\rho(q,p,t) + \{\rho(q,p,t), H(q,p)\} = 0", color=WHITE)

            axes.c2p(0, 1)
        ]
        
        self.play(
            *[particle.animate.move_to(pos) for particle, pos in zip(particles, new_positions)],
            run_time=2

        # Poincaré Recurrence

            FadeOut(liouville_title),
```

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class AdaptiveQuadrature(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Set colors (blue and green with gold for adaptive)
        function_color = GREEN
        uniform_color = BLUE
        adaptive_color = GOLD
        
        # Title
        title = Text("The Power of Adaptive Quadrature", font_size=32)
        title.to_edge(UP)
        
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Set up axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4],
            y_range=[0, 2],
        ).scale(0.7)
        axes.center()
        
        # Define a function with a sharp spike - ideal for showing adaptive advantage
        def func(x):
            return np.exp(-0.5 * (x - 1)**2) + 0.8 * np.exp(-8 * (x - 3)**2)
        
        # Plot the function
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: func(x), color=function_color)
        
        graph_label = Text("Function with irregular behavior", font_size=20)
        graph_label.next_to(axes, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph), Write(graph_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show uniform grid approach (equal spacing)
        uniform_rects = VGroup()
        x_min, x_max = 0, 4
        num_uniform = 8
        dx_uniform = (x_max - x_min) / num_uniform
        
        for i in range(num_uniform):
            x = x_min + i * dx_uniform
            height = func(x)
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=dx_uniform,
                height=height,
                fill_color=uniform_color,
                fill_opacity=0.4,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x + dx_uniform/2, height/2), aligned_edge=ORIGIN)
            uniform_rects.add(rect)
        
        uniform_label = Text("Uniform Grid: Equal spacing everywhere", 
                           font_size=20, color=uniform_color)
        uniform_label.next_to(graph_label, DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(uniform_rects), Write(uniform_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clear uniform grid and show adaptive approach
        self.play(FadeOut(uniform_rects), FadeOut(uniform_label))
        
        # Adaptive approach - fewer rectangles in smooth areas, more near the spike
        adaptive_rects = VGroup()
        
        # Fewer rectangles in smoother regions
        for i in range(3):
            x = 0 + i * (2/3)
            height = func(x)
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=2/3,
                height=height,
                fill_color=adaptive_color,
                fill_opacity=0.4,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x + (2/3)/2, height/2), aligned_edge=ORIGIN)
            adaptive_rects.add(rect)
        
        # More rectangles near the spike
        for i in range(8):
            x = 2 + i * (2/8)
            height = func(x)
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=2/8,
                height=height,
                fill_color=adaptive_color,
                fill_opacity=0.4,
                stroke_width=1
            )
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(x + (2/8)/2, height/2), aligned_edge=ORIGIN)
            adaptive_rects.add(rect)
        
        adaptive_label = Text("Adaptive Quadrature: Focus on complex areas", 
                            font_size=20, color=adaptive_color)
        adaptive_label.next_to(graph_label, DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(adaptive_rects), Write(adaptive_label))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Show conclusion

        )
```

```python
    def create_simple_grid_circuit(self, rows, cols, color):
        # Create a grid of squares representing circuit components
        grid = VGroup()
        gates = VGroup()
        
        # Create gates
        for i in range(rows):
            for j in range(cols):
                gate = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_opacity=0.7, fill_color=color)
                gate.move_to([j - cols/2 + 0.5, i - rows/2 + 0.5, 0])
                gates.add(gate)
        
        # Create connections
        connections = VGroup()
        for i in range(rows):
            for j in range(cols):
                idx = i * cols + j
                
                # Horizontal connection (if not last column)
                if j < cols - 1:
                    line = Line(
                        gates[idx].get_right(),
                        gates[idx + 1].get_left(),
                        stroke_width=2
                    )
                    connections.add(line)
                
                # Vertical connection (if not last row)
                if i < rows - 1:
                    line = Line(
                        gates[idx].get_bottom(),
                        gates[idx + cols].get_top(),
                        stroke_width=2
                    )
                    connections.add(line)
        
        grid.add(gates, connections)
        return grid
    
    def create_simple_circuit_representation(self, text, color):
        # Create a simple circuit representation with text
        circuit = VGroup()
        
        # Main component
        gate = Circle(radius=0.6, fill_opacity=0.7, fill_color=color)
        gate_text = Text(text, font_size=16).move_to(gate.get_center())
        
        # Input and output
        input_line = Line(LEFT, gate.get_left(), stroke_width=2)
        output_line = Line(gate.get_right(), RIGHT, stroke_width=2)
        
        circuit.add(gate, gate_text, input_line, output_line)
        return circuit
```

```python
                x, y = r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta)

        manifold_text.to_edge(UP)

        self.play(Create(circle), Create(manifold))

        # Show the symplectic form as a grid pattern

        # Create concentric circles to represent the symplectic form
        for r in np.linspace(1, 3, 3):

            symplectic_grid.add(circle_arc)

            x, y = 3 * np.cos(angle), 3 * np.sin(angle)

            position = dot.get_center()
            r = np.sqrt(position[0]**2 + position[1]**2)
            if r > 0.1:  # Avoid division by zero near the origin
                direction = [-position[1]/r, position[0]/r, 0]
                arrow = Arrow(start=position, end=np.array(position) + 0.5 * np.array(direction), color=YELLOW)
```

```python
            start_x, end_x = -4, 4
```

```python
            color=LIGHT_GRAY,

            x = self.x_pos(v)
            tick = Line([x, -0.1, 0], [x, 0.1, 0], stroke_width=2, color=GRAY)
            num = Text(str(v), font_size=20, color=GRAY).move_to([x, -0.35, 0])

                fill_color=BLUE_D,
                fill_opacity=0.85,
                stroke_color=BLUE_B,
            ).move_to([x, 0.525, 0])

        )

    @beat("Place the fulcrum at the computed expected value", seconds=3)
```

```python
import numpy as np

class RefractionExplainer(ForgeScene):

    @beat("Set up the glass boundary and incoming ray", seconds=4)
    def setup_scene(self):
        # Boundary line between air and glass (horizontal line at y = 0)
        self.boundary = Line(LEFT * 6, RIGHT * 6, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Labels for media
        self.air_label = Text("Air (n₁ ≈ 1.0)", font_size=24, color=BLUE_A).to_edge(UP).shift(LEFT * 3)
        self.glass_label = Text("Glass (n₂ ≈ 1.5)", font_size=24, color=TEAL_A).to_edge(DOWN).shift(LEFT * 3)
        
        # Glass region background
        self.glass_bg = Rectangle(
            width=14, height=4, 
            fill_color=BLUE_E, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0
        ).shift(DOWN * 2)

        # Incoming ray (top-left to origin)
        # Angle of incidence around 45 degrees
        self.p_start = np.array([-4.0, 3.0, 0.0])
        self.p_origin = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
        
        self.incident_ray = Arrow(
            self.p_start, self.p_origin, 
            buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4
        )
        self.incident_label = Text("Incident Ray", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).move_to(np.array([-2.8, 1.8, 0]))

        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.glass_bg),
            Create(self.boundary),
            Write(self.air_label),
            Write(self.glass_label),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(self.incident_ray),
            FadeIn(self.incident_label),
            run_time=2.0
        )

    @beat("Draw the normal line perpendicular to the boundary", seconds=4)
    def draw_normal(self):
        # Normal line passing through the point of incidence
        self.normal_line = DashedLine(UP * 2.5, DOWN * 2.5, color=GREY, stroke_width=2)
        self.normal_label = Text("Normal", font_size=18, color=GREY).move_to(UP * 2.7 + RIGHT * 0.5)

        self.play(
            Create(self.normal_line),
            Write(self.normal_label),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(2.0)

    @beat("Highlight the angle of incidence", seconds=4)
    def show_incidence_angle(self):
        # Angle between normal (UP) and incident ray reversed (-direction)
        # Vector is from origin to p_start: [-4, 3] -> normalized: [-0.8, 0.6]
        # Angle with UP [0, 1] is about 53.13 degrees
        self.arc_i = Arc(
            radius=0.8,
            start_angle=PI/2,
            angle=-np.arctan2(4, 3), # angle from UP vector clockwise
            color=YELLOW_C,
            stroke_width=3
        ).move_to(ORIGIN, aligned_edge=RIGHT) # Adjusted visual centering for arc
        
        # Better: use Angle utility or explicit arc
        # Let's create a clean arc between normal (UP) and incident vector (-direction)
        v_inc = (self.p_start - self.p_origin)
        v_inc = v_inc / np.linalg.norm(v_inc)
        
        # Using ArcBetweenPoints or standard Arc
        self.angle_i_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.7, 
            start_angle=np.pi/2, 
            angle=-np.arccos(np.dot(UP, -v_inc)),
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        self.label_i = MathTex(r"\theta_1", color=YELLOW, font_size=28).move_to(np.array([-0.4, 0.6, 0]))

        self.play(
            Create(self.angle_i_arc),
            Write(self.label_i),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

    @beat("Show the refracted ray bending towards the normal", seconds=5)
    def show_refraction(self):
        # Refracted ray in glass bends more towards the normal (steeper down)
        # Let's compute refracted angle using Snell's Law: n1 * sin(theta1) = n2 * sin(theta2)
        n1 = 1.0
        n2 = 1.5
        # Incident angle theta1 = arccos(dot(UP, -v_inc))
        v_inc = (self.p_start - self.p_origin)
        v_inc = v_inc / np.linalg.norm(v_inc)
        cos_i = np.dot(UP, -v_inc)
        sin_i = np.sqrt(max(0.0, 1.0 - cos_i**2))
        
        sin_r = (n1 / n2) * sin_i
        theta_r = np.arcsin(sin_r)
        
        # Direction vector in glass (going down and right, but steeper down along -UP)
        # angle from downward normal (DOWN) is theta_r
        dx = np.sin(theta_r) * np.sign(-v_inc[0]) # keep same side
        dy = -np.cos(theta_r)
        v_ref = np.array([dx, dy, 0.0])
        
        self.p_end = self.p_origin + v_ref * 3.75
        self.refracted_ray = Arrow(
            self.p_origin, self.p_end, 
            buff=0, color=RED_C, stroke_width=4
        )
        self.refracted_label = Text("Refracted Ray", font_size=20, color=RED_C).move_to(np.array([1.8, -1.5, 0]))

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(self.refracted_ray),
            FadeIn(self.refracted_label),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(2.5)

    @beat("Highlight the angle of refraction", seconds=4)
    def show_refraction_angle(self):
        # Arc for refracted angle between DOWN vector and refracted ray
        v_ref = (self.p_end - self.p_origin)
        v_ref = v_ref / np.linalg.norm(v_ref)
        
        cos_r = np.dot(DOWN, v_ref)
        theta_r = np.arccos(cos_r)
        
        self.angle_r_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.7,
            start_angle=-np.pi/2,
            angle=theta_r if v_ref[0] > 0 else -theta_r,
            color=RED_C
        )
        
        self.label_r = MathTex(r"\theta_2", color=RED_C, font_size=28).move_to(np.array([0.4, -0.6, 0]))

        self.play(
            Create(self.angle_r_arc),
            Write(self.label_r),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(2.0)

    @beat("Introduce Snell's Law equation", seconds=5)
    def show_snells_law(self):
        self.snell_formula = MathTex(
            r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)",
            font_size=36
        ).to_edge(UP).shift(RIGHT * 3.5)
        
        self.play(
            Write(self.snell_formula),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Add a bounding box to emphasize the formula
        self.formula_box = SurroundingRectangle(self.snell_formula, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(self.formula_box), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(2.0)

    @beat("Explain why it bends: wave wavefront view", seconds=5)
    def explain_speed_change(self):
        # Show wavefronts slowing down on entering the medium
        self.explanation_text = Text(
            "Light slows down in denser medium,\ncausing the wavefronts to pivot.",
            font_size=20,
            color=LIGHT_GRAY

        # Draw a few parallel wavefront lines perpendicular to the incident ray
```

```python
import numpy as np

class GaussianNoiseAnimation(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        signal_color = "#3498db"  # Cool blue for signal
        noise_color = "#7f8c8d"   # Muted gray for noise
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Illuminating Signals Through Gaussian Noise", font_size=28)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Element 1: Create axes and clean sine wave
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
        ).scale(0.8)
        axes.move_to(ORIGIN)
        
        # Original clean signal
        def clean_signal(x):
            return np.sin(x)
        
        clean_graph = axes.plot(clean_signal, color=signal_color)
        clean_label = Text("Clean Signal", font_size=24, color=signal_color).next_to(axes, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(clean_graph))
        self.play(Write(clean_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Element 2: Add Gaussian noise
        x_vals = np.linspace(0, 6, 25)
        y_vals = [clean_signal(x) + np.random.normal(0, 0.5) for x in x_vals]
        noisy_dots = VGroup()
        
        for i in range(len(x_vals)):
            dot = Dot(point=axes.c2p(x_vals[i], y_vals[i]), color=noise_color, radius=0.05)
            noisy_dots.add(dot)
        
        noise_label = Text("Signal with Gaussian Noise", font_size=24, color=noise_color).next_to(axes, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(clean_label))
        self.play(Write(noise_label))
        self.play(Create(noisy_dots))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Element 3: Show signal and noise equation
        equation = MathTex("y(t) = x(t) + n(t)")
        equation.next_to(axes, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Element 4: Show SNR equation
        snr_eq = MathTex("SNR = \\frac{P_{signal}}{P_{noise}}")
        snr_eq.next_to(equation, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(snr_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clear screen
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(clean_graph),
            FadeOut(noisy_dots),
            FadeOut(noise_label),
            FadeOut(equation),
            FadeOut(snr_eq)
        )
        
        # Element 5: Show Gaussian distribution
        gaussian_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1],
        ).scale(0.8)
        
        # Gaussian function
        def gaussian(x, mu=0, sigma=1):
            return (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mu) / sigma) ** 2)
        
        gaussian_graph = gaussian_axes.plot(lambda x: gaussian(x), color=noise_color)
        gaussian_label = Text("Gaussian Noise Distribution", font_size=24).next_to(gaussian_axes, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(gaussian_axes))
        self.play(Create(gaussian_graph))
        self.play(Write(gaussian_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show Gaussian distribution equation
        gaussian_eq = MathTex("n(t) \\sim \\mathcal{N}(0, \\sigma^2)")
        gaussian_eq.next_to(gaussian_axes, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(gaussian_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Element 6: Conclusion
        self.play(
            FadeOut(gaussian_axes),
            FadeOut(gaussian_graph),
            FadeOut(gaussian_label),
            FadeOut(gaussian_eq)
        )
        
        conclusion = Text("As noise variance increases, SNR decreases", font_size=28)
        conclusion.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=1)
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final fade out
```
